zero warnings on Basic, Empty, Expandable, Resizable, KitchenSink and
EngineSwap. Adds jsdom, @testing-library/react and the SWC React plugin to run
component tests.

refactor(frontend): groupColumns returns the type it actually produces

The deferred review item, done properly rather than patched.

groupColumnsRecursive builds `{key, title, children}` group columns and both it
and the public groupColumns declared `ColumnDef<T>[]`, which is leaf-only. That
compiled because a group is structurally assignable to a leaf — every extra
field is optional — so the wrong type was never going to be caught by tsc. Both
signatures now say ColumnDefs<T>, the union the function has always returned.

My first attempt cascaded into "implicitly any" errors at the sort callbacks and
I backed it out. That was self-inflicted: I changed the annotation without
importing ColumnDefs, so `result` became an error type and everything reading it
degraded. ColumnDefs is an array of a union, not a union of arrays, so inference
is fine once the name resolves.

countLeafColumns went with it. It took ColumnDef<T>[] and cast each entry to
reveal a `children` field the type denied having; it now takes the union and
asks isColumnGroupDef, which is the same question without the cast.

fix(frontend): make the CSV headers match the rows they label

The last open review item. Papa is handed {fields: headers, data: rows} and
reads row[field] for every header, so the header list and createTraceObject are
one contract. They had drifted: headers came from the visible column titles,
which include the "Evaluators" group and its children, and createTraceObject
emits none of those — evaluator metrics come from traceAnnotationInfoAtomFamily,
not the trace row. Every such header wrote an empty column, and conversely any
key the visible columns omitted was dropped without a word.

Deriving headers from columns could never have changed the data, because the row
mapper does not consult columns at all — it could only misalign it. So headers
now come from what the mapper actually emits, narrowed to the columns still
visible and kept in the mapper's order. Hiding a column still drops it from the
CSV; showing one the mapper cannot fill no longer invents a blank one.

Pinned with a test in the package that owns the mapper: the emitted keys must
equal DEFAULT_TRACE_EXPORT_HEADERS exactly, and every promised header must be
present in the row. That is the contract the writer depends on, and it is what
would have caught this.

docs(frontend): plan for the /evaluations render loop

Diagnosed but not fixed. The console stack shows composeRefs recursing through

fix(frontend): pin one immer instance so table state can draft Maps

Opening /evaluations died with "Maximum update depth exceeded" on reload. The
cause was two immer copies: oss and ee depend on immer 10, which is where
`enableMapSet()` runs, but @agenta/ui declared jotai-immer without declaring
immer, so pnpm resolved that peer to immer 11 — a second instance where the
plugin was never enabled.

`columnVisibilityStateAtom` holds a Map of Maps, so every viewport-visibility
write went through immer 11 and threw. The throw tore down the table chrome,
and React's repeated attempts to re-render that subtree produced the update
loop. It only showed on reload because a first paint writes no visibility
state yet.

Three changes, smallest first: @agenta/ui now declares immer, a workspace
override pins a single version (following the @tanstack/query-core precedent
already in that file), and `enableMapSet()` moved into the atom module that
owns the Map. That last one matters beyond this bug — only web/oss called it,
so /m, Storybook and tests each hit the same crash on their first write.

refactor(frontend): keep tooltip triggers off other triggers' elements

Three call sites handed SimpleTooltip a child that was itself an asChild Radix
trigger, so both collapsed onto one button and Radix composed their refs into

tooltip because React's onFocus bubbles from the child.

This is hygiene, not a bug fix. It was the prime suspect for the /evaluations
loop and it was wrong: the repro tests here pass with and without the change,
and un-nesting all three did not clear the page. The real cause was a second
immer instance. The tests stay because they pin the structural property — the
live DOM had `data-slot="tooltip-trigger"` sitting on the trigger button, and
the guard fails if that returns.

feat(frontend): export evaluator metrics in the traces CSV

Turning on evaluator columns and hitting Export produced a CSV without them
and no indication anything was dropped. Two reasons: the header list is fixed
and carries no evaluator entries, and the header selection is title-based
while evaluator leaf columns have `title: null` (the header cell is hidden and
the cell draws its own label), so it could not see them even in principle.

The metrics are correlated data, not row data — they live on annotations
linked to a span. `exportMatchingTraces` gained an optional `enrich` transform
that runs after dedup and the cap, so nothing is fetched for a row that will
not be written, and the join happens there: one annotations request per chunk
for every invocation link at once, never one per row. That per-chunk property
is what made this feasible at all and is the first thing the tests pin.

Enrichment belongs in a transform rather than in `flushBatch` because the sink
is the format boundary: anything done there cannot be reused by a different
sink and sits outside the loop's cancellation path.

fix(frontend): review findings from the observability stack

Six issues raised on #5954-#5958, each verified against the code first.

`getNodeById` walked `Object.values(node)`, which visits every property rather
than just `children`. Span metadata carries `span_id` too — an annotation
span's `invocationIds` points at a different span — so a single-node lookup
could return that bag instead of the span. The regression test covers exactly
that shape; it passes on an array input either way, which is why the first
version of it caught nothing.

Both annotation queries scoped their request by `projectId` but not their
cache key, so a project switch with the same links reused the previous
project's annotations. The drawer store had inherited the same mistake when it
stopped calling the oss wrapper that resolved the project internally.

Session token and cost totals used `||` down their fallback chains, so a real
incremental total of 0 fell through to the cumulative one and double-counted a
span that reported no new tokens.

`getOperator` can return undefined for an operator in the union but missing
from OPERATORS; dereferencing `hidesValue` threw during validation and took
the dialog's render with it.

Plus two small ones: the docs link opened without `noopener`, and a
secondary-only empty state rendered an orphaned "Or" separator.

fix(frontend): make the day grid keyboard-operable and the span chips theme-safe

Two findings from the #5958 and #5957 reviews.

The date picker's calendar was reachable but not usable without a mouse: every
day carried `tabIndex={-1}` and no key handler existed, so a keyboard user
could open the popover and go no further. It also declared `role="grid"` while
rendering one flat list of cells with no rows.

It now uses a roving tabindex — one day in the tab order at a time — with
arrows moving by day and by week, Home/End along the week, PageUp/PageDown by
month, and Enter or Space to select. Stepping past either edge pages the view
so arrows never dead-end at a boundary. The flat cell list is chunked into
`role="row"` weeks, which is what makes the row-wise moves mean anything.

`spanTypeStyles` mapped its colours to `--ant-*`, which antd's ConfigProvider
emits at runtime. On an antd-free host those resolve to nothing, so the span
chips lost their background and text colour entirely on /m. Every value is now
a generated `--ag-*` token: the `preset-*` hue pairs already exist in
palette.ts with their own dark values, so no new tokens were needed.

The keyboard tests fail against the previous implementation — all four — which
is the only reason to trust them.

that would mislead whoever ran them next.

The rest are smaller but the same kind: `spanTypeStyles` was assigned to WP2 in

the DateRangePicker brief told the agent to add a direct dayjs dependency while
the shipped component takes it through `@agenta/shared/utils/dateTime`; and
`FilterTagsInput` appeared in the export handoff with no track owning it.

branch. They now use repository-relative paths and tell the session to confirm

fix(frontend): the tool drawer invalidates every key a connection touches

`ConnectDrawer` kept its own `invalidateConnections` that hit only
["tools","connections"] and ["tools","catalog"], while the shared hook in

saying why: gateway_connections rows back the triggers list. So connecting a

`assertHostQueryClient` had tests; `getHostQueryClient()` — the accessor every

The JSDoc on the assertion still described the pre-migration failure mode

real failure is a host that installs one client and hydrates another: two

fix(frontend): mount the mobile session workspace's two halves exactly once

The phone layout and the tablet layout were two sibling containers, one `md:hidden`
and the other `hidden md:block`. Both are only CSS-hidden, so neither unmounts, and
`{chat}` and `{pane}` each mounted twice — two conversation engines running at every
viewport.

Both widths now drive the SAME SplitPane, so each half exists once and a rotation
across the md breakpoint no longer remounts the conversation mid-stream. Expressing
"one pane takes the full width" needed a `paneGrow` prop on SplitPane: the driven
pane is `grow-0` with a controlled flex-basis, so it cannot fill on its own.

fix(frontend): keep the UTC designator on every analytics range

`sorted` was built as UTC and then had its designator stripped
(`toISOString().split(".")[0]`). `fetchDashboardAnalytics` reparses that string with
`dayjs()`, which reads a bare timestamp as LOCAL time, so every preset window was
skewed by the viewer's offset. The new test fails against the old code with
"expected 180 to be less than 2" — 180 minutes is exactly UTC+3.

Three call sites computed the same string by hand; they now go through
`resolveRangePreset` / `toRangeInstant`. "all time" resolved to an empty string that
the same fetch throws on, so it gets a real epoch start, which also retires the
sentinel the UI package kept as a workaround.

Also: `loading` no longer reads `isPending`, which is true forever for a disabled
query and pinned every usage card to its skeleton before a project resolved. And
four bucket fields nothing produces or reads are gone, including the `enviornment`
misspelling that had no way to be right.

fix(frontend): follow OS appearance changes, and stop feeding click events to reload

The "system" theme listener responded to an OS change by setting the mode to
"system" — the value it already held. React bails out of an equal write, so nothing
recomputed and the page only flipped on reload. The OS preference is now its own
state, which also removes a `matchMedia` read from the render path.

DataTable passed `onReload` straight to `onClick`, so a handler like SWR's `mutate`
received the MouseEvent as its first argument and wrote it into the cache as the new
data. It is now called with no arguments.

Clickable rows also take focus and answer Enter/Space. They looked like buttons and
behaved like buttons for a mouse only.

fix(frontend): ask before deleting a schedule or a subscription

Both sections deleted (and revoked) outright. The `confirm` seam they needed already
existed and was already supplied by both hosts for the connection sections — those
two just never took it. Wired on the desktop (AlertPopup) and on /m (the confirm
sheet).

The confirm type had been copied into four files and drifted: one typed `onOk` as
`() => Promise<void>`, rejecting a synchronous handler there and nowhere else. It
now has one definition.

Also in the tools surface: the OAuth popup poll outlived the modal (untracked
interval, no unmount cleanup), a failed create was swallowed with only a spinner
reset, a rejected refresh left the row silently unchanged, and `confirm` was missing
from two dependency arrays, so a host that changed it kept the first one forever.

fix(frontend): give the agent config header the OSS commit host adapter

The agent path renders the shared `AgentConfigHeader`, which owns the commit button
itself. It was passed neither `appId` nor the two callbacks, so an agent commit
skipped this app's out-of-band caches (the variant registry and the evaluator
tables) and its onboarding event, leaving those lists stale.

The adapter moved out of the OSS button wrapper into `useCommitHostAdapter`, so the
wrapper and the header share one definition rather than a second copy.

The commit button's dirty guard also only covered its own button: a host trigger
passed as `children` was cloned with `onClick` alone, so it could open the modal on a
clean revision. And two theme fixes in the same components, both of which rendered a
fixed light value in dark mode: a hardcoded white header background and a raw cyan
`--ag-c-*` literal.

fix(frontend): stop waiting badges sticking on after the last session clears

The per-agent waiting counts were derived from a list query that keeps the previous
key's pages (`placeholderData: keepPreviousData`) and holds them once the query goes
disabled. When the last waiting session cleared, the id set emptied, the query
switched off, and the old pages kept every badge lit — permanently.

Also in the sessions surface: the list card's "View all" dropped the agent it was
scoped to and landed on the project-wide list; the filter sheet's Clear cleared the
agent even on an agent-scoped page, silently widening it past the page it belongs
to; a long-press timer outlived a tab closed under the finger; the status chips
claimed to be a `<nav>`; and the Filters button had no hover or focus state.

Build/Chat mode is persisted now — which of the two you work in is a standing
preference, not something to relitigate on every reload.

fix(frontend): do not clear a composer's attachments when the navigation fails

Both mobile composers stashed the task, cleared the staged files, and then awaited
`router.push`. A push that rejects left the attachments gone, the task stashed for a
route that never mounted (so it replays the next time that session id opens), and no
error anywhere. They now navigate first, drop the stash on failure, and clear only
once the destination is committed to. The create-agent action does the same and
releases its latch, which otherwise stayed engaged for the rest of the mount.

`LiveConversation`'s pending-task guard was a bare flag on a component that survives
a session switch, so the next session's stashed task was swallowed. It holds the
session it fired for.

The composer also guards against concurrent sends — Enter, the send button and a
completing voice take could all fire while an upload was in flight.

In the shared home composer: a selected agent that leaves the list no longer sticks
(the trigger went blank and the task went to an agent that is gone), a rejected
`onStart` reaches the host instead of becoming an unhandled rejection, and the
create-agent latch is module-scoped, as its own comment already claimed.

`AgentNameInline` drops its two antd imports, and its rename pen becomes a real
button — the only other way in was a double-click.

refactor(frontend): move profile, webhooks and API keys onto the Fern client

Three axios modules migrated to the generated resource clients, with accessors added
for users, keys and webhooks.

The profile response was cast straight to `User`; it is validated with zod now, which
is what Fern's `unknown` return demands. The 401-as-signed-out path reads Fern's
`statusCode` rather than an axios `response.status`.

The keys and webhooks routes take scope parameters the spec does not declare, so
`workspace_id` / `project_id` ride along as `queryParams` — dropping them would have
silently listed and minted keys against the wrong workspace.

Fern types the webhook list and count fields as optional while the local types promise
them, so the boundary defaults them. That mismatch was real, not a typing nuisance: a
consumer mapping over `subscriptions` would have hit undefined.

fix(frontend): stop the mobile settings surfaces losing what you typed

Editing a webhook subscription sent `event_types: [first]`, so a subscription created
on the desktop or through the API lost every event type but one the moment it was
saved here. The sheet holds the full list now and narrows it only when you actively
pick a different event, and says so when it is holding types it cannot show.

The rename field could not be cleared: it rendered `value || project.project_name`,
so emptying it put the old name straight back, and Save then sent the name you had
just deleted. The sheet owns its draft and seeds it on open.

The secret-reveal Copy button reported success unconditionally — `navigator.clipboard`
is undefined outside a secure context and the optional chain swallowed it. On a secret
the backend shows exactly once. It now reports the failure and tells you to copy by
hand.

Billing checkout opened its window after an await, which mobile browsers block: the
portal navigates this tab, and the desktop pricing modal opens its tab inside the
click and fills in the URL when it arrives.

Also: `?tab=tools` rendered the tools section even where the env gate disables it; a
confirmation sheet survived a tab switch and would have acted on the section you left;
a deep-linked tab flashed Preferences before the router was ready; the usage bar
warned "at limit" whenever the limit was zero or unknown; a plan with no base amount
rendered "$undefined /month"; and MembersTab's `canWrite` was renamed to what it
actually tests, which is that we know the workspace, not that you may write to it.

docs(frontend): triage the CodeRabbit findings on the sessions-UX stack

128 review comments across 18 PRs, written before any were actioned so the work could
be scoped, then updated with what was fixed, what turned out not to be a defect, and
what is knowingly partial.

Every referenced file still exists, which is a weak signal: all three Criticals were
verified and they split three ways — one real double-mount, one already fixed, one an
artifact of how the stack is ordered.

docs(frontend): record the live verification of the CodeRabbit fixes

The analytics probe narrows the timezone claim. The backend echoes the same UTC
instant for the bare and the Z-suffixed input, so the queried window was always
right and the designator carries no wire risk. The damage was the client-side
reparse: 1620 minutes instead of 1440 for the 24-hour preset, which picked 60-minute
buckets and week-scale tick labels.

docs(frontend): record the browser verification, and correct a dark-mode claim

The double-mount is confirmed by counting mounted nodes with the fix and with
SessionWorkspace reverted: two composers and two Lexical editors before, one each
after. The webhook event-type loss and the rename field are confirmed against real
data.

One claim was wrong. AgentConfigHeader's `--ag-c-FFFFFF` does not render white in
dark mode; the compat shim is theme-aware and resolves to the same #141414 as the
token that replaced it. That edit is hygiene, not a fix. The cyan icon literal beside
it IS theme-blind, so that half stands.

fix(frontend): render one template-detail shell, not both

Same defect the mobile session workspace had. `identity`, `meta` and `body` are
element variables shared by a phone shell (`lg:hidden`) and a desktop shell
(`hidden lg:flex`). Both stay in the DOM, so React mounted each of them twice: the
host's markdown renderer parsed the whole AGENTS.md twice on every render, and the
Use button existed twice at every width.

Confirmed in the browser on /m — the template detail rendered two "Use" buttons
before the fix, one after.

Only the matching shell is built now, chosen by the same `useMediaQuery` seam the
session workspace uses. The hook sits above the `!template` early return, since a
hook cannot follow one.

chore(frontend): make the repo pass its own format and lint checks

`pnpm run format` and `turbo run lint` were failing on this branch before any of the
recent work — CI's last green-checked commit predates it. Nine files were unformatted
(three `eslint.config.mjs`, the token-generation script, and several test files), and
the package test suites carried import-order and `type`-vs-`interface` violations the
lint rules reject.

The count looks alarming locally ("2643 files") only because the check globs the whole
tree and picks up `mobile/.next` build output, which does not exist on a fresh
checkout. The real set is the nine above.

fix(frontend): delete the app-layer re-export shims and repair the orphaned tests

`turbo run lint` and the web unit layer both failed on this branch before any recent
work. Three separate causes, all from earlier carve waves rather than one bug.

The trace-drawer extraction left 40 pure re-export modules in `oss/src` pointing at
`@agenta/observability{,-ui}`. OSS lint bans exactly that (`no-restricted-syntax`:
consumers must import from the source package for tree-shaking). Every importer now
names the package directly and the shims are gone; the handful that imported a
shim's `default` take the package's named export instead, since the packages have no
default.

Five OSS test files were orphaned when their subjects moved into `@agenta/chat`:
`attachments.test.ts` and `toolFormat.test.ts` test modules that no longer exist here
and are already covered in the package, so they are deleted. `partToolName` moved
too, so its block goes with it. `ApprovalDock`'s two suites now take
`getPendingApprovals` from `@agenta/chat/model`, and their mocks of
`@agenta/entities/workflow` and `jotai` were missing members the package code reaches
for — the jotai mock is partial now, so it stops going stale every time the dock
composes one more package hook.

The entity-import smoke test used `await import()` inside each case, putting a cold
transform of a very large module graph inside the per-test timeout: fine alone (~22s),
past 60s under the full suite. The imports are static now, so the transform happens
during collection where no per-test timeout applies.

Verified: `pnpm run lint` exits 0 across the workspace, OSS and EE `tsc` are clean,
and the web unit layer passes.

fix(ci): copy every workspace package into the mobile image

The mobile image hand-listed the six packages it thought it linked, and that list
fell behind the real closure: mobile now needs 22 workspace packages, 15 of which
were never copied. `@agenta/chat` imports `@agenta/entity-ui/tool-permission`,
entity-ui was not on the list, and the build died with

    error TS2307: Cannot find module '@agenta/entity-ui/tool-permission'

on a subpath that resolves fine in every other environment. Both architectures have
failed on this since the packages grew past the list.

It now uses the same `COPY --parents packages/*/package.json` + `COPY packages/`
pair the oss and ee images already use. Turbo still builds only what
`--filter=@agenta/mobile` needs; the difference is that nothing has to remember to
update a list when a package gains a dependency.

docs(frontend): make the sessions-UX runbooks safe to actually follow

Fourteen review findings against the stack runbooks, mostly commands that fail or
lie when run.

Three TypeScript gates counted `error TS` lines inside a command substitution. That
takes the pipeline's status from `grep` rather than `pnpm`, so a compiler that
crashed, OOM'd or never ran reported a count of zero and passed. All three now run
`tsc` directly under `set -euo pipefail`.

`execute-stacked-prs.md` selected commits as "the newest 50" one paragraph after
saying the commits are not contiguous — a positional slice both picks up other
people's commits and drops session ones. It selects by range now. Its lane
creation used `git checkout -b`, which fails outright on the 29 lane branches its
own Phase 1 finds; `-B` resets them instead. Phase 5 told operators to fix a PR base
with `gh pr edit`, which the same document's trap list records as broken on this repo
— it uses the `gh api -X PATCH` route now. And the stash-isolation section never
mentioned that `git stash -u` keeps untracked files in a third parent, so restoring
from `<stash>` alone silently drops every new file.

`restack-onto-112.md` and `plan.md` are marked historical and point at the runbook
that records what was actually done: their figures (88 commits, no lane branches, no
PRs, 17 mobile type errors) were all overtaken. `restack` also advised amending a
lower lane to add an upper lane's delta, which rewrites a commit every lane above
already builds on; it says make a new commit on the upper lane. One `pkg/settings-spine`
SHA had a space in the middle of it (`675003 3`).

`plan-settings-nav-takeover.md` told the implementer to drop the `NavDrawer` header in
takeover mode. Below `lg` the sidebar IS that drawer, so following it leaves a phone
with no way to open the settings navigation — the takeover would hide what it took
over. The shipped `SettingsScreen.tsx` keeps the row, and the plan now says why.

fix(frontend): read the SSO flags the way the backend reads them

`SsoProvidersSection` tested `flags.is_enabled !== false` and `flags.is_valid !== false`.
The backend's enable-SSO gate is `(provider.flags or {}).get("is_active") and
.get("is_valid")` — a different flag for the first, and the opposite default for both:
an omitted flag means NOT active there and meant active here. A provider the backend
refuses to enable SSO with was rendered as enabled and verified.

The access tab returned `null` for loading, for a failed query and for an
organization with no flags alike, so a slow or failed request was a blank tab with
nothing to read and nothing to press. It has the three designed states now, in the
`states/` folder the other mobile features use.

The flag save never finished its lifecycle: the success tick was set and never
cleared, so it sat on the last-saved row for the rest of the session, and a failed
save was swallowed entirely — the switch flipped back on refetch and that was the
only signal. It clears after three seconds and surfaces the failure.

Smaller ones: a domain whose `created_at` will not parse rendered "Invalid Date" and,
because NaN compares false against everything, never read as expired either; the
tooltip that carries the only explanation of what each toggle does hung off a `<span>`,
so it was mouse-only; and `DataTable` rendered its trailing actions column whenever
`actions` was passed, leaving a dead 48px column on every read-only host. (`RowActions`
already returned null for an empty menu, so there was no stray trigger — only the
column.)

fix(frontend): reset the project dialogs on every close, drop a needless cast

The create dialog reset its form only in `onCancel`, so closing it by actually
creating a project left the name and the make-default switch sitting there for the
next open. Both dialogs reset in `afterClose` now, which fires however the modal
closed.

`NamedSecretTable` handed its delete dialog `selectedSecret as unknown as
LlmProvider`. `NamedSecretRow extends LlmProvider`, so the value was already
assignable — the double assertion bought nothing and would have hidden a genuine
mismatch if the two types ever drifted apart.

refactor(frontend): move the API-key list onto a scoped query atom

`useApiKeys` fetched with `useEffect` + `useState` + a manual promise chain, which the
frontend conventions rule out for data fetching. It showed: every mount refetched,
each surface showing keys kept its own copy of the list, `remove` spliced the row out
of local state rather than refetching, and a failed list was swallowed into
`console.error`.

It reads `apiKeysQueryAtomFamily` now — keyed by workspace AND project, because the
request is scoped by both, so switching either re-keys the query on its own. Mutations
invalidate through `getHostQueryClient()` rather than writing rows by hand.

`listing` reads `fetchStatus`, not `isPending`: a disabled query (no workspace
resolved yet) stays pending forever and would have pinned the table to its loading
state. `@agenta/settings` gains the same query peers `@agenta/observability` and
`@agenta/sessions` already declare; jotai was already a peer here.

fix(frontend): theme the last fixed colours, gate the disabled settings tabs

The code editor's scrollbar was `#ddd` on `#f0f0f0` — invisible against a dark
editor; both read theme tokens now. Two more fixed literals go with them: the
`--ag-c-FFFFFF` in the agent operations header and the copied-toast tick, which was
pinned to `--ant-lime-6` (a token that only exists where antd's ConfigProvider
mounts, so it resolved to nothing on `/m`).

Tools and Triggers are gated at the render boundary as well as in the tab resolver.
The resolver already redirects a disabled `?tab=tools`, but a render boundary that
trusts the router is one refactor away from rendering a surface this deployment
turned off.

The template strip's storage key takes the `agenta:` prefix every other key in this
app uses; "the prototype spelled it differently" was not a reason to opt out. The
`previewUrl` ownership note named `DriveExplorer`, which only reads it —
`useImagePreviews` derives and revokes it. The jotai peer floor moves off `>=2.0.0`,
which was never true of anything this repo tests: the apps run 2.16.

The triage document records the three findings that are NOT actionable at the call
site, with the evidence: the mount download has no Fern method to route through, the
secret sheets cannot adopt "empty means keep stored" because the write path throws on
a missing key, and the sidebar grouping reads as correct.

merge: the v0.112 drift remediation into the mobile extraction lane

Measured against this lane the drift branch was two commits, not the 68 it showed
against `fix/package-query-client`: 66 of them had already landed on the sessions
lanes and arrived when those lanes were merged. The docs commit was already present,
so this is the one remaining code commit, 137 files.

Eighteen files conflicted. Neither side was a superset, so they were resolved
individually rather than by preferring a branch:

- `TemplateDetail` — drift adds a `layout` prop (toolbar/rail) but still renders both
  shells. Took drift's file and re-applied the single-shell fix on top, so the markdown
  body is built once.
- `data-table` and `ProjectsPage` — drift's versions already carry the argument-less
  `onReload()` and keyboard-activated rows, so they were taken whole. A partial
  resolution had left them referencing `visibleActions` and `rowActions`, which do not
  exist on this side.
- `AgentOverviewScreen` — both hunks are one structural change (the shared page-width
  cap replacing `ContentRail`), so they had to move together.
- `useSidebarDynamicChildren` — the merged body is drift's, which drops group labels;
  keeping our hunk would have orphaned `groupsAreInformative`.

Two regressions the merge introduced, both fixed here:

- `AnalyticsDashboard` went back to `${formatNumber(failure_rate)}%` on a 0-1 fraction,
  so a 5% failure rate read as "0.05%". Drift had fixed this and a later merge from the
  stale `fix/package-query-client` lineage undid it.
- `gatewayTrigger/state/invalidate.ts` reached for the `queryClient` singleton, which
  the host-client rule bans: `/m` installs its own client, so those writes land in an
  orphan cache and do nothing. It resolves per call now.

fix(frontend): slide the collapsing panes instead of resizing their contents

Two faults, both measured.

RightPanelSplit never animated at all. It detected the flip with useState and a
render-phase setPrevOpen — React re-renders before committing when you set state
during render, and that re-render sees prevOpen === open, so `justToggled` was
always false in the committed output and `holdAnimate` only arrived in an effect,
after the new width had painted. Opening the Files pane fired zero flex-basis
transition events. A ref survives into the commit (the shape MainLayout already
uses). Its `barClassName` also declared its own [transition:height_…], which
lands after SplitPane's slide in the class merge and silently dropped the bar's
flex-basis transition; that class now names both properties.

The bigger one: animating the width reflowed everything inside. As the pane
narrowed, its contents saw a new width every frame — file tiles reflowed into
fewer columns, labels rewrapped, the column grew taller than the pane. The motion
drew attention to exactly what it should have hidden.

So translate instead of resize. For the duration of the slide the pane's content
leaves the flow at a FIXED pixel width — the width it had while open — pinned to
the edge the box collapses towards (right for a start-side pane, left for an
end-side one). The box still animates flex-basis, so the layout reclaims the
space and the fill still grows, but the content being clipped never changes
width, so the shrink reads as a translation. Static and responsive again the
moment the slide ends, because during a DRAG the reflow IS the feedback.

before the listener runs — and both commands build their query from a
`Router.query` the other has not committed yet. So the pair raced, whichever
survived dropped the other's key, and the observed order was even reversed (span
logged before trace). One `patchQuery({trace, span})` is one command and one
navigation, so there is nothing to race.

Fixed, both verified by sampling `location.search` every 25ms through a click:

1. The click wrote `trace` and `span` as two `useQueryParamState` calls.
   `requestNavigationAtom` is a single slot, so the second command replaced the
   first before the listener ran, and both `Router.replace`s built their query
   from a `Router.query` the other had not committed. `Router.replace` returned
   FALSE (cancelled) and the URL kept one key. Now one `patchQuery({trace, span})`.
2. The `selectedTraceId -> setTraceParam` effect fired ~50ms behind the click with

   A ref marks the selection the click already queued so the effect skips it.

With those two, the URL correctly reads `?trace=…&span=…` about 70ms after the
click — measured, where before it never held both.

The wiper is `setSpanParam(undefined)` from ObservabilityTable's own cleanup
effect (caught with a stack trace), whose guard is `!traceParam && !selectedTraceId`
— it reads "nothing is selected" because `traceParam` goes EMPTY again after the
params landed. Guarding that branch on the in-flight ref was not enough: the ref
clears when the URL first matches, and `traceParam` empties after that. Why
`traceParam` — i.e. `appStateSnapshotAtom.query` — drops the params it just
received is the next thing to find. Note `state/appState/` and `state/url/` are

fix(frontend): the trace drawer's query seams read a stale router snapshot

The drawer now opens on a row click and stays open, with ?trace and ?span both
on the URL. Verified by sampling location.search + the drawer node every 25ms
through a click: `?trace=` and the drawer at 393ms, `&span=` added at 2424ms,
both still there at 10s. Before, the params landed and were wiped ~300ms later
and the drawer went with them.

The seams bound in Providers.tsx rebuilt the WHOLE query from `router.query`:

    const query = {...router.query}          // ← a render-time snapshot
    delete query.trace; delete query.span
    router.push({pathname: router.pathname, query}, ...)

They are rebound every render, but each callback still closes over that render's
query. Invoked shortly after another navigation, they rebuilt the URL from a copy
that predated it and dropped the keys that had just landed — so the click wrote
both params and the drawer's own seam immediately pushed a query from before the
click. Both seams now mutate the LIVE `location.search`, which has no snapshot to
go stale.

This was the third of three causes, all of them read-modify-write races on the
URL; the other two are in the previous two commits.

   present, not on a param CHANGE. It now remembers the trace it last acted on and
   does not reopen a closed drawer for the same one, so the loop cannot form

fix(frontend): restore the chat bubble's 32px avatar column and per-line code blocks

Two parity defects found by driving a live run against deployed v0.112.1.

ChatBubble shrink-wrapped its avatar slot to the avatar's own 24px, where the
antd-x Bubble it replaces reserves 32px around the same 24px avatar - so every
message body sat 8px inboard of the desktop app's, on both placements. The
component's docstring claimed the metrics mirrored antd-x; the 12px gap did, the
column did not.

Fenced code blocks rendered every line on one row ("a = 1b = 2c = 3").
streamdown@2.5.0 renders one span per Shiki line but classes it only when
lineNumbers is on, and that class is what carries `block`; we pass
lineNumbers={false}, so the lines stayed inline. Make the line spans blocks in
MD_CLASS instead.

Also records WP-1 in the parity inventory, including the two open design calls
(the 9px splitter gutter, the markdown block scale) and the harness fixes: a
DPR pin for tab resolution, an align mode for vrt.py, and a chat-body strip.

fix(frontend): restore the desktop app's markdown scale and rhythm in chat

Arda's call after the WP-1 comparison: the Streamdown swap had shrunk every
block. Base was 12/13px against the desktop app's 14, h1 14 against 16, and
every block's bottom margin was zeroed in favour of one 8px wrapper gap, so
headings, lists, quotes and tables all sat the same distance apart and a
two-column table stretched the full bubble width.

Rhythm is measured off v0.112.1's rendered blocks, not copied from its margins:
Streamdown wraps each block in its own div, so sibling margins cannot collapse
the way antd-x's did. The root gap is zero and each block owns only the space
below it, which reproduces the collapsed gaps exactly and can never double up.
Nested lists and paragraphs inside list items or blockquotes are exempt - they
were inflating the block around them.

Verified live against prod, boundary by boundary: 12 / 4 / 14 / 14 / 8 / 12,
base 14, h1 16, h2 14, table auto-width.

fix(frontend): honour closeOnLayoutClick so drawers stop dismissing on outside clicks

EnhancedDrawer declared closeOnLayoutClick and its docstring listed it as
covered, but those were its only two mentions - never destructured, never read,
and no ...rest to forward it. Dismissal was gated solely on maskClosable, which
defaults to true, and all 13 drawers that pass closeOnLayoutClick={false} pass
no maskClosable. Every one of them dismissed on a stray outside click despite
asking not to, losing typed input on the form ones.

The docstring is where the mistake lives: it read the name as closes on layout
click and concluded Radix made it redundant, missing that every call site passes
false to SUPPRESS dismissal. Derive dismissOnOutside = closeOnLayoutClick ??
maskClosable so an explicit value wins and maskClosable stays the fallback.

Verified with a two-build control rather than by reading: same trace drawer,
same outside click on the rail, prod (unfixed) closes and local (fixed) stays

fix(frontend): restore the selected state on the time-range picker

Prioritised WP-3 by lane churn: the agenta-ui diff against 112.2 is dominated by
files the lane MOVED into the package, and date-range-picker (633 lines) was the
biggest interactive one.

The Observability range panel gave no indication of which range was applied.
Prod paints the active row with the primary fill; local painted nothing, and the
first row showed the browser's blue focus ring instead of the app's. 112.2
renders this from Filters/Sort.tsx, which sets popupSelectedItem when sort
matches, so the extraction dropped it.

The state was never wrong - aria-checked reads true at runtime and the JSX
already branches on it. The bug is one layer down: @agenta/ui/styles exports a cn
that is a plain concatenator while @agenta/ui/components/ui/utils exports one
built on extendTailwindMerge. rowClassName set bg-transparent unconditionally and
bg-secondary conditionally, which only works under tailwind-merge; with the
concatenator both classes land and CSS order left every row transparent.

Fixed by making the base conditional rather than swapping cn, which would start
deduping every other class in the file and needs its own verification. Also gave
the rows the kit focus treatment, since they are real buttons where prod's were
inert divs and preflight is off.

Verified live. Checked the blast radius too: 35 files import the non-merging cn,
three combine conditional and unconditional colour classes, and all three are
safe on inspection - so this was the only live instance.

docs: the reference moved - prod is 112.2 and this branch is 113 commits behind

Two premises this inventory rested on were wrong, both now checked rather than
assumed.

Prod is not v0.112.1. The rail stamps v0.112.2 and has done for every capture
from 14:02 onward, compared pixel-wise across six prod shots. That does not
invalidate the comparisons - it makes most of them stronger, since comparing
against prod was comparing against 112.2 - and it resolves the places I wrote
'112.2 has X, prod lacks it, so prod is older': prod runs a 112.2 build, not
necessarily the tip.

The same-environment guard's tell died with that premise. With both builds on
112.2 the version stamp no longer discriminates; on three real pairs it was only
working on incidental sidebar pixels. shot.sh now writes the source URL beside

session came back FIRST — so the screen resolved another session's agent,
another session's revision, and cached the answer for the full 60s
staleTime.

Only the fallback is removed. A missing row stays null, because that is a
real answer for a session with no turns yet; what is not an answer is a
different session's row.

A `/sessions/query` row carries BOTH `id` and `session_id`, and they are
different values: `id` is the session STREAM id (v7, what the route
carries), `session_id` is a v4 and something else. `useAgentEntity` filtered
by `sessionIds: [routeId]` and then matched `row.session_id === routeId`.
Measured against the running API: the filter returns ZERO rows for a route
id, and the match would not have hit even if it had.

It never surfaced because the miss fell through to `?? rows[0]` — so every
session silently resolved the FIRST row's agent and revision. Removing that
fallback earlier tonight is what turned a wrong answer into a visible empty
one, which is how this became findable at all.

still accepted. Verified on a session that was read-only a minute ago —

could not reach them. So TurnMetrics and a new TurnTimestamp now live in

fix(chat): make elicitation work on /m, and stop a host opting out of it by accident

/m rendered NOTHING for a client tool. An elicitation ('what is your favourite
colour?') showed only a 'Waiting for your answers' line, with no form to answer, no

The widgets themselves were app-layer, so the move splits them by what they depend on:
the dispatcher and predicate go to @agenta/chat/clientTools (antd-free, so /m can ship
it — its package contract test enforces that), and the widgets go to
@agenta/entity-ui/clientTools, because the elicitation form is SchemaForm whose state
engine is antd Form.

The dispatcher reaches the widgets by VALUE, not by registering them as a module side
effect. The side-effect version looked right and failed silently: both packages declare
sideEffects:false, so the bare import was tree-shaken, the registry stayed empty, and
every elicitation auto-settled as 'not handled by this client'.

Composer lock: /m derived 'waiting on the user' from pending APPROVALS only. hitlPending
already covers both gates and parked client tools, so the hook now returns it and /m
uses it for the composer placeholder and the status line.

Also gives @agenta/entity-ui the JSX transform its own vitest config predicted it would
need — the moved elicitation render test is the .tsx suite it warned about.

fix(chat): give /m the jump-to-latest pill, from the desktop's own component

Scrolling back through a transcript on /m left you to scroll all the way down again by
hand. Prod floats a 'Jump to latest' pill once you leave the newest turn.

The pill was app-layer in oss, so it moves to @agenta/ui as ChatJumpToLatest and both
transcripts render it.

/m also had no state to drive it: useTranscriptAutoScroll tracked 'am I near the bottom'
in a REF, deliberately, so following appends causes no re-render. That fact now also
mirrors into state, which is the half a rendered control needs.

ScreenScaffold gains a scrollOverlay slot for it. The pill cannot live inside the
scroller — an absolutely positioned child of a scrolling box scrolls away with the
content — so the slot wraps the scroller in a positioned frame, and only when something
is actually passed, leaving every other screen's box exactly as it was.

fix(mobile): mount the trace drawer for the whole app, not just Observability

'View trace' on a chat turn did nothing. The drawer opens through an ATOM, so whoever
renders it decides where it works — and /m rendered it inside the Observability screen
alone. The action set the atom on a session page where no drawer existed. web/oss mounts
it globally in AppGlobalWrappers for exactly this reason.

The router seams move with it: they have to be bound wherever the drawer can open, not
only where the traces table lives.

fix(chat): give /m the turn toolbar's own chrome, and pin the shadow across Tailwind majors

The revealed toolbar on /m was loose text floating over the transcript. Prod puts it in
an elevated bordered card so it reads as a control surface and does not sit transparently
on top of streamed text. That chrome was a literal class string in the oss message
component, so it becomes turnToolbarClass in @agenta/ui beside the reveal and row classes
it belongs with, and both hosts use it.

The shadow inside it is spelled out instead of `shadow-sm`. This string ships to two apps
on DIFFERENT Tailwind majors: v4 renamed the scale, so v4's `shadow-sm` is v3's `shadow`,
and /m rendered a visibly heavier drop (0.1 alpha, 3px blur) than the desktop's (0.05,
2px). Measured both; they now match exactly.

/m also had the user-side toolbar at right-10, which is the assistant offset mirrored
rather than prod's right-2 under the bubble.

fix(mobile): let a turn be rewound, the way the desktop already can

A turn on /m offered Copy and View trace but no way to go back and re-run from it. Prod
puts a rewind on every turn but the last: on a user turn it truncates the conversation
and hands the message back to the composer to edit; on an assistant turn it regenerates.

useAgentConversation has exposed `rewind` all along — it SCANS and returns a plan, and
deliberately opens no dialogs, leaving the surface to warn and to refill the composer.
/m simply never called it. It now does, with the same warning when tools that already ran
would be rewound past (rewinding cannot undo them) and the same composer refill.

The composer's input handle becomes an optional host-owned ref for that refill; it keeps
its own when nothing is passed.

fix(mobile): send the run's project on invoke, so an agent resolves its own connection

Every agent run on /m failed with "connection '<slug>' not found for provider
'anthropic'", as if the vault secret were missing. It was not: the connection exists in
the project, and the same agent runs fine on oss/ee.

The run was resolving against the WRONG PROJECT. buildAgentRequest appends project_id to
the invoke URL only alongside an Authorization header, and /m registered no auth-header
provider — so it sent

    /invoke?application_id=…                       (/m, before)
    /invoke?application_id=…&project_id=…          (prod)

The backend takes a request's project from that query param and, with none, falls back to
the caller's DEFAULT project. The runner then read the default project's vault, found no
connection with the agent's slug, and reported the agent's own connection missing.

web/oss registers the provider in DeferredAppBoot; /m now does the same at the providers
root. The token comes from a new getAccessToken in @agenta/auth rather than a second
SuperTokens call, since /m already runs that recipe.

Verified live: the invoke URL now carries project_id and the agent replies (23.3s, 29.1K,
$0.072717) where it previously errored.

fix(mobile): stop announcing a run the user is already watching

/m grew a bar above the transcript on every turn — a 'running' chip and a Stop — that
appeared when the run started and vanished when it ended, shifting the transcript twice
per run. It also put a second Stop on screen: the composer's send button is already one.

The desktop shows this only for a run THIS browser is not driving (another tab, another
device), where the transcript would otherwise look frozen, and docks it above the composer
with the approval and interaction strips rather than putting it on top. /m showed it for
`running || streamingHere` — its own turns included — and in a header bar.

So the condition narrows to `running && !streamingHere` and it moves down with the other
strips. The strip itself moves from web/oss into @agenta/chat/components so both surfaces
render one component; it gains an optional trailing action, which is how /m keeps the
cross-device Stop the desktop's version has no equivalent for.

Verified live on /m: streaming a turn now shows no bar, no layout shift, and the composer's
send button as the only Stop. The running-elsewhere branch is NOT live-verified — local
runs finish inside the liveness poll interval, so the second tab never caught the window.

fix(mobile): put the working indicator in the turn, and give /m the startup narration

Two halves of one gap. /m rendered the loading dots as a status line AFTER the whole turn
list, so on a tall pane they floated far below the avatar they belonged to, detached from
anything. And they were wordless: the runner narrates what it is doing while the
environment boots (#6047, 'Starting the agent' / 'Agent ready') so a ~15s cold start reads
as progress rather than a stalled session — /m dropped that narration entirely.

The desktop renders the started-but-empty turn as the turn itself: avatar plus the label,
in the bubble. /m now does the same, under the same gate (assistant turn, streaming, no
content yet), and the status line keeps only the PARKED case it still owns.

The lifecycle system was app-layer in oss, so it moves to @agenta/chat rather than getting
a second implementation: startupPhases (the wire-label parser), turnClock (the per-session
label atoms plus useStartupPhase), and TurnActivity (StartupActivity / WorkingDots /
WaitingForInput). useAgentConversation now feeds the label from its own onData and clears
it on every terminal status, which is what the desktop hook already did and the reason /m
had nothing to show.

@agenta/chat also gets the JSX transform its vitest config predicted it would need — the
moved render test is the .tsx suite that note was about.

Verified live on /m: the indicator now reads 'Starting the agent' at the same y as its turn
row, beside the avatar, instead of below the list.

fix(mobile): let a wrong sign-in verdict be corrected

A transient 401 stranded a perfectly valid session on the sign-in page until a hard
reload. Observed directly: /m sitting on /auth while /api/projects returned 200 with the
full project list.

Two independent faults made it permanent.

The verdict was wrong to begin with. fetchProjects collapsed 'the refresh could not reach
the backend' into the same false as 'the session is revoked', so an API that is up but not
yet serving — it answers 401, and the refresh that follows fails for the same reason — read
exactly like a sign-out. refreshSessionOutcome now reports which of the three things
happened, and an unreachable refresh is reported as the transient error it is.

And nothing could correct it. The gate ran its query only OFF /auth, and this app sets
refetchOnWindowFocus: false, so once bounced there was no re-check trigger at all —
staleTime marks data stale, it does not schedule anything. The gate now keeps asking on
/auth, re-asks on focus, and routes both ways: a confirmed session sitting on the sign-in
page is handed back to the root resolver. The routing is a pure function so the guards that
stop it looping — and the one that never forwards out of the OIDC callback mid-exchange —
are tested rather than argued about.

Not live-verified: reproducing it needs a session that 401s once and then recovers, and the
local session has since genuinely expired. Covered by unit tests instead.

feat(frontend): one sign-in for oss, ee and /m — shell, flow and rules

The sign-in UI was already shared (@agenta/auth-ui): the desktop's auth components are thin
wrappers over the package's forms. The FLOW was not. 760 lines of orchestration lived in the
oss page, so /m had no email-first discovery, no org SSO, no returning-visitor promotion and
no invite capture — it rendered whatever the env flags enabled and stopped there.

Three layers move down.

@agenta/auth (React-free, so the rules are unit-tested): signInPolicy derives what the screen
offers — deriveEntry (promotion of the remembered provider or email, the heading), deriveMethods
and soleSsoRedirect, the rule for redirecting into a lone SSO connection without asking.
discovery widens to the whole /auth/discover payload rather than its sso slice, with abort as a
first-class outcome, and the narrow discoverSsoProviders it supersedes is deleted. Plus
mapAuthError, readInviteParams and readAuthConfig, which mirrors getEffectiveAuthConfig field
for field including the AUTH_EMAIL_ENABLED-without-a-mode case getEmailSignInMode collapses.

@agenta/auth-ui: useSignInFlow, the entry → methods → code machine both pages now drive —
discovery with cancellation, the SSO redirect and its org-slug memo, invite capture, the
interrupted code attempt, message auto-clear. Everything app-shaped is a seam, because the
OIDC transport genuinely differs: the desktop redirects to its registered callback URI, /m
routes through a cookie. AuthShell joins it as the frame (560px method column beside the
marketing panel, which hides itself below lg), so /m stops being a second layout — the logo
strip is positioned rather than stacked, which also fixes a form that centered on the space
left under it instead of on the viewport.

deriveMethods deliberately follows the deployment's AUTHN_EMAIL rather than the discovered
per-email flags, matching what the page did inline: discovery adds org SSO on top, it does not
switch an install between passwords and codes.

The page keeps what is genuinely its own — region selector, auth-upgrade org switching, invite
email-mismatch, its antd rendering — and drops from 760 lines to 465. /m gains the whole flow
and loses SsoDiscoveryForm, since SSO now falls out of discovery instead of hiding behind its
own entry point.

Two notes. oss never called configureAuth, so the package would have thrown on render reading
env and the API host; configureAuthPackage is the side-effect module the page imports (ee
re-exports that page, so both are covered). And the hook reads config on mount, not during
render: /m resolves env at runtime, so deriving from it in the first pass fails hydration.

Verified on /m against the local stack: entry → discover (200) → password step with the address
locked → back to entry, and a real sign-in. oss/ee is type- and lint-clean but unrun here — it
needs a SuperTokens stack.

chore(mobile): /m moves to Next 16, oss and ee stay on 15

Next 16 makes Turbopack the default bundler for `next build`, which hard-fails
when a webpack config is present, and it removes or renames several config
surfaces. Mobile is Pages Router, so the headline breaking change — async
`params`/`searchParams`/`cookies()`/`headers()` — does not apply, and neither do
parallel-route defaults, PPR, or the async image/sitemap props. That leaves a
small, mechanical set of changes:

- `eslint.ignoreDuringBuilds` is a removed config option; `next build` no longer
  lints, and the type gate already runs as its own turbo task.
- `turbopack.root` was gated to development. Turbopack now drives the build too,
  so the workspace root has to apply unconditionally or the monorepo misresolves.
- The `webpack.IgnorePlugin` that silenced the AI SDK's optional zod-alternative
  peers becomes `turbopack.resolveAlias` onto an empty module. The SDK guards
  those adapters with try/catch, so both spellings land in the same place.
- `middleware.ts` becomes `proxy.ts` and the export is renamed. The gate is pure
  header/cookie/URL logic, so it ports unchanged to proxy's Node-only runtime.
- `jsx: preserve` becomes `react-jsx`, and `next-env.d.ts` regenerates.

Only `@agenta/playground-ui`'s `next: <16` peer actually objected; the pnpm
`next@<15.5.18` overrides never capped anything, since a `^16` request does not
match that selector. Both majors coexist cleanly: oss, ee, storybook and every
shared package stay on 15.5.x with no peer warnings, and both desktop builds pass.

Verified: mobile builds on Turbopack with no warnings and keeps its standalone
output layout, tsc and the unit suite are green, and the oss and ee builds are
unaffected. `next dev` and the proxy's runtime behaviour against a live request
are not yet exercised.

fix(ui): pin a list's group headings below the panel header, not on top of it

On a phone viewport the sessions panel showed 'WAITING ON YOU' drawn over
'Sessions · 3 waiting', with a row's text visible through both.

Two faults, one surface. PanelSection's header and SessionCardList's group heading
were both `sticky top-0 z-10` in the SAME scroller, so they pinned to the same line
and overlapped. And the heading's `bg-inherit` had nothing opaque to inherit —
PanelSection's body set no surface — so it resolved transparent and rows scrolled
visibly through it.

The heading now pins at `--ag-panel-header-h`, which PanelSection measures from its
own header and publishes. Measured rather than a constant: the variants are different
heights (40px page, 48px rail, both measured live) and the header wraps on a narrow
viewport, so any hardcoded offset is wrong somewhere. The 0px fallback keeps hosts
WITHOUT a header of their own — the session-history popover, the full sessions list —
pinning at the top exactly as before, so no caller has to opt in.

The body now states its surface, which is what makes `bg-inherit` opaque.

Verified live at 430x932 that the header pins and rows scroll under it on an opaque
surface. NOT verified: the corrected offset itself — the dev server went down before I
could see the heading pin at 40px, and an earlier attempt of mine was wrong here (it
removed the stickiness instead of offsetting it), so treat this as needing a look.

The @agenta/oss build OOMs at the 4096 MB cap on this branch's package
graph (both archs, two runs). Same change lands on release/v0.113.0 via
#6162; identical lines merge clean.

fix(web): break the workspace package cycle that hangs the production build

`next build` of @agenta/oss died in "Creating an optimized production build"
with `uncaughtException RangeError: Invalid array length at Array.push`, and
with a 4096 MB cap it died as a heap OOM instead. No stack, no module name,
both CI arches, and reproducible locally. A bisect named 805792a8b2 (client
tool elicitation on /m).

That commit moved the client-tool widgets into @agenta/entity-ui, and the
widgets import @agenta/chat (skin types and resolvers) and @agenta/settings-ui
(`useToolsConnections`). Both packages already depend on @agenta/entity-ui, so
the workspace graph gained its first two dependency cycles.

The loop: pnpm links a workspace dependency as a symlink under
`<pkg>/node_modules/@agenta/<dep>`, so a cycle makes a directory tree of
unbounded depth. Webpack's `FileSystemInfo` hashes a context directory by
walking it recursively and resolves each symlink to its absolute target before
it recurses, so the walk ping-pongs between the two package directories and
never ends. A wrapper around `Array.prototype.push` caught the throw at the
call site:

    [pin-stack] push failed; this.length = 134217728 args.length = 1
        at bundle5.js:29:303117
        at FileSystemInfo._getUnresolvedContextTsh (bundle5.js:29:274683)
        at processQueue (bundle5.js:29:1448574)

The fix removes both cycles and keeps the behaviour the culprit commit added:

  - The client-tool contract (`ClientToolMeta`, `SettleClientTool`,
    `ClientToolWidgetProps`, `ClientToolWidget`) moves DOWN to
    @agenta/shared/clientTools, beside `CLIENT_TOOL_DESCRIPTORS`.
    @agenta/chat/skin re-exports every one, so hosts and skins keep their
    import site.
  - `useToolsConnections` moves DOWN to @agenta/entities/gatewayTool, beside
    the connection API calls it wraps. @agenta/settings-ui re-exports it, so
    its public API is unchanged.
  - @agenta/entity-ui's clientTools registry drops the `registerChatSkin`
    side-effect call and the two resolvers it re-exported (nothing imported
    them). The dispatcher still reaches the widgets by VALUE, and its lookup
    still checks the registered store before that fallback, so a host override
    keeps winning. No host registers client-tool widgets today.
  - The elicitation "Asked by ..." label is now resolved by the dispatcher and
    passed as `askerLabel`, because the tool-display store lives in
    @agenta/chat and the widget must not import it back.
  - @agenta/entity-ui drops its @agenta/chat and @agenta/settings-ui
    dependencies. @agenta/shared gains `ai` (types only, optional peer).

Adds `agenta-shared/tests/unit/workspaceGraph.test.ts`: the @agenta/* graph
must stay acyclic. Nothing else catches this class of bug. TypeScript, ESLint,
and every unit test pass with the cycle in place, the dev server runs fine, and
only the production build dies, without saying why.

Verified: `next build` of @agenta/oss and of @agenta/mobile both complete;
tsc --noEmit clean for oss, ee and mobile; unit tests green for shared (362),
chat (364), entity-ui (473) and entities (1330). Reintroducing the
entity-ui -> chat dependency makes the new test fail with
"Workspace dependency cycle: @agenta/entity-ui -> @agenta/chat -> @agenta/entity-ui".

composer, disables the composer, and parks the first-run seed until a key lands.

The chain closes on the gate from the previous commit: first submit creates the

Trade-off against desktop: desktop mints an EPHEMERAL client-only agent and
commits it on send, so abandoning the hero leaves nothing behind. Here the first

fix(frontend): keep the chat composer above the phone keyboard

On a phone browser the on-screen keyboard opens over the page instead of
resizing it. The playground frame is `h-dvh`, and `100dvh` measures the layout
viewport, which the keyboard does not shrink. The bottom of that frame is the
chat composer, and the frame is `overflow-hidden` and exactly as tall as the
layout viewport, so the page cannot scroll to reveal it either.

Two mechanisms, one per browser family:

- The app served no `<meta name="viewport">` of its own, so it got Next's
  default `width=device-width`. Adding `interactive-widget=resizes-content`
  makes Chrome and Android shrink the layout viewport for the keyboard, so
  `dvh` follows and the composer stays visible.
- iOS Safari ignores that directive. `useVisualViewportHeight` tracks
  `visualViewport` and publishes the visible height as `--ag-viewport-height`,
  which the playground frame now sizes against with a `100dvh` fallback.

The hook is idle unless a keyboard-sized inset is present, so desktop and
Android keep their exact current height. Sending on a touch device now blurs
the editor, which closes the keyboard and returns the page to full height.
Desktop keeps focus after Enter, guarded by `(pointer: coarse)`.

fix(frontend): start a phone in the chat view, not the configuration

On a phone the playground opens on the configuration pane and the transcript is
off-screen, so a new agent's first message lands somewhere the user cannot see.
The pane asks for 300-440px and the transcript for 420px more, so the two
cannot share a phone screen at all.

`configPanelCollapsedAtom` defaulted to `false` (pane visible) for everyone. A
plain boolean cannot tell "I want the config pane" apart from "I have never
said", so the default could not vary by device without overruling a real
preference. The stored value is now tri-state: `null` means nothing is stored,
and it resolves to hidden on a phone and visible everywhere else.

A stored preference still wins in both directions, and the `»` reveal button in
the chat header stores one, so a phone user who wants the configuration is one
tap away and stays there. `getOnInit` makes a stored preference apply to the
first paint instead of one render later.

fix(mobile): hold the parked first message until the vault answers

The connect-model gate reports `gateActive: false` while the vault query is still

fix(chat): wait out a workflow that has not loaded its invocation URL (M3)

The first message to a newly created agent failed on /m with "This agent workflow
has no invocation URL — it can't be run yet." The same agent ran from the desktop
a minute later, and from /m on retry.

Root cause: the shared chat engine's `prepareSendMessagesRequest` threw on the FIRST
null from `buildAgentRequest`. Null there does not mean "not runnable" — it means the
workflow entity carrying `data.url`/`data.uri` has not been fetched yet. The first-run
hand-off navigates, resolves the agent's latest revision over the network, and fires
the stashed message as soon as the transcript settles, which is often before that
entity lands. The desktop never hit it because `useAgentChatSession` has bounded the
same build since #6042; the shared hook the mobile app uses never got that fix.

So give both surfaces one copy: `boundedRequest` moves from the oss chat slice into
`@agenta/chat/assets`, the shared engine wraps its build in it, and the desktop
imports it from the package. A not-yet-loaded workflow now retries for up to 15s and
fails with a clear message if the URL never appears, instead of failing instantly.

fix(frontend): keep the /m composer above the phone keyboard and close it on send

Reported on Chrome, Pixel 8 Pro, at /m. Two halves: opening the keyboard does
not move the page up, so the composer is partly covered; and after Enter the
keyboard stays open instead of returning the layout to normal.

The mobile app was never covered by the earlier desktop fix (#6169). It serves
its own viewport meta, `width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover`,
with no `interactive-widget`. Without that directive Android Chrome opens the
keyboard OVER the page: the layout viewport keeps its full height, so the three
`h-dvh` frames keep theirs, and the composer at the bottom of the chat column
sits under the keyboard with no way to scroll it into view.

The meta now sets `interactive-widget=resizes-content`, which makes the keyboard
shrink the layout viewport so `dvh` follows it. That is the whole fix on Android.
`viewport-fit=cover` stays because this app draws real safe-area insets.

iOS Safari ignores the directive, so `useVisualViewportHeight` mounts once in
`_app` and publishes the visible height as `--ag-viewport-height`. ScreenScaffold,
AppShell and SessionWorkspace read it with a `100dvh` fallback, so the Android
path is unaffected: with the layout viewport already shrunk the measured inset is
zero and the variable is never set.

For the second half, the composer now blurs after a send on touch devices, which
closes the keyboard and returns the frame to full height. Both send paths are
covered: plain Enter and the send button both route through `submitEditorAsMarkdown`
with the same `onSubmit`, and that is the function this wraps.

The blur has to be DEFERRED. `submitEditorAsMarkdown` clears the editor on the
statement after it calls `onSubmit`, and that update reconciles a fresh DOM
selection, which re-focuses the contenteditable and reopens the keyboard. The
editor's own docs already record it: "a focused editor re-asserts its selection
on the next reconcile".

The height variable also clears on `focusout`, not only on a visual-viewport
resize. Some iOS builds close the keyboard silently, which would leave the page
pinned short with dead space under the composer.

RichChatInput composer, and it sits inside `Layout.tsx`'s `h-[calc(100dvh-29px)]`

testsets and observability. The evaluator playground, the human-evaluation

The hook now runs once in the shared `Layout`, which wraps every route in both

Also fixes the blur after send, which never took effect. `submitEditorAsMarkdown`

reopens the keyboard. `dismissSoftKeyboardAfterSend` defers the blur past that
reconcile. The editor already documents the behaviour: "a focused editor
re-asserts its selection on the next reconcile".

fix(frontend): stop the evaluation run page minting an atom per read

Opening an evaluation run with real data threw React error #185, "Maximum
update depth exceeded", and the error boundary replaced the page.

jotai's atomFamily keys its cache by REFERENCE unless given an areEqual: 2.20's
implementation is a plain atoms.get(param) against a Map. Every family in
EvalRunDetails is keyed by an object literal rebuilt at the call site, e.g.
scenarioColumnValues.ts:485 does

    get(scenarioStepsQueryFamily({scenarioId, runId}))

so the Map never hits and each call mints a brand-new atom. For the query
families that is self-driving: each generation mounts its own observer, the
observer emits, the emit invalidates the atom that created it, and the re-read
mints the next generation. React counts an update per generation and throws.

Measured on a seeded 25-scenario non-terminal run, where ~200 cells should
create ~200 atoms once:

    before   2.5s   486 column-value atoms,  1504 step-query atoms
             20s   3244 column-value atoms, 10744 step-query atoms, climbing
    after    2.5s   144 column-value atoms,    24 step-query atoms
             20s    144 column-value atoms,    24 step-query atoms, flat

This is why it never reproduced on an empty project: the steps query is gated
on enabled: Boolean(effectiveRunId && batcher && scenarioId), so with no
scenarios nothing reads the family. A non-terminal run makes it worse, because
refetchInterval 5000 keeps every generation's observer emitting.

The atoms themselves are byte-identical to v0.112.3. The extraction (#6065)
replaced the antd table with the virtualized engine, which re-renders cells far
more, and that is what pushed a latent churn over React's update-depth limit.

Adds sameFamilyKey and passes it to the 24 object-keyed families across 9
files. Families keyed by a plain string are left alone: an areEqual makes jotai
walk the Map linearly instead of hashing, so it would be a regression there.

fix(frontend): stop the evaluations list looping on evaluator metric columns

Opening /evaluations threw React error #185, "Maximum update depth exceeded",
and the error boundary replaced the page. It only happened once a run carried
`data.mappings` that produce evaluator METRIC columns, which is why an empty
project never reproduced it.

`setOutputTypesMap` notified its listeners unconditionally:

    outputTypesCache.set(key, map)
    globalVersion += 1
    listeners.forEach((listener) => listener())

Its only caller is the metric GROUP header, which rebuilds the map from the
evaluator's schema on render and passes a NEW Map with the SAME content every
time. `useEvaluationRunsColumns` subscribes to that key and its listener calls
`setOutputTypesVersion(v => v + 1)`, so:

    write -> notify -> setState -> re-render -> rebuild map -> write -> notify -> ...

An infinite synchronous loop through a module-level cache, which is exactly what
React reports: a component sets state from an effect whose dependency changes on
every render. The metric columns arm it because the group header is the only
caller.

The fix is to make the write idempotent: compare the map's content and return
early, without bumping the version or notifying, when nothing changed.

Worth recording, because every stack trace pointed elsewhere: the reported error
always surfaced inside Radix's `composeRefs` under `ColumnVisibilityTrigger`
(`dispatchSetState <- setRef <- Array.map <- ... <- safelyDetachRef <-
commitDeletionEffectsOnFiber`). That is where the loop SURFACES, not where it
starts — the churning columns remount the header subtrees and Radix detaches
composed refs during the deletion. Five hypotheses in the table chrome were
eliminated by experiment before instrumenting identity changes showed the hook's
inputs were all stable (rows 3, everything else 1-2 changes across 129 renders)
while its output churned 69 times, which led back through `isMetricHidden` and
`outputTypesVersion` to this write.

Verified on a dev build against a real EE API, with six seeded runs whose
mappings produce metric columns:

    before   crashed, 0 rows, 0 headers
    after    6 rows, and the metric columns render for the first time —
             "Contains JSON", "Exact Match", "Quality Rating", each with
             Score and Verdict
    after a reload with column-visibility state persisted: still clean

Six tests on the rule the loop violated; two are red without the guard.

fix(frontend): collapse the duplicate antd instance that unthemes EE UI

The post-signup survey rendered a white card with an almost invisible
Continue button whenever the app was in dark mode. The card's own styling
was correct: it reads --ant-color-bg-elevated, and on <html> that variable
holds the dark value. The variable was being redefined underneath it.

The survey's <form> carries antd's `css-var-root` class, and the page ships
a token block for that class holding antd's STOCK defaults
(--ant-color-primary:#1677ff, --ant-form-label-color:rgba(0,0,0,0.88)) —
not our palette, in either theme. Those components never see our
ConfigProvider, so they fall back to antd's built-in light theme and
override every --ant-* token for their whole subtree.

They cannot see it because there were two physical antd packages. antd
takes an optional date-fns peer, and `web/ee` resolved date-fns@3.6.0 while
`oss`, `mobile`, `storybook` and every @agenta/* package resolved
date-fns@4.4.0, so pnpm materialised antd twice. A single EE build then
bundles both: files under web/oss/src resolve the oss copy, files under
web/ee/src resolve the ee copy. ConfigProvider's React context belongs to
one copy and is invisible to the other, which is why exactly the ten EE
files that import antd directly render unthemed.

The date-fns split came from @tremor/react, which pulls date-fns@3.6.0 via
react-day-picker@8. It is declared in both web/ee and web/oss and imported
nowhere in the repo — the `tremor-*` names in the Tailwind config are local
token names, not package references. Dropping it leaves one antd and one
date-fns, and ee, oss and packages/agenta-ui now resolve the same path
under node_modules/.pnpm.

fix(frontend): remove the five polynomial-time regexes CodeQL flagged

The email check, the git-remote URL parsing and the JSON fence check each let two quantifiers
compete for the same characters, so a long non-matching input made the engine retry every split
point. Measured on the old patterns: 16s for a fence padded with 5000 spaces, 604ms for a path
of 40k slashes.

Each rewrite is a character walk or a set of non-overlapping patterns, and each comes with a
test that runs the old pattern and the new code over the same table of inputs.

Alerts 296, 297, 298, 299, 300 (js/polynomial-redos).

fix(frontend): check organization ids before they reach a request URL

An organization, workspace or project id that carried ../, ? or a whole second URL moved the
request off the endpoint the caller meant to hit. Both requests now pass their ids through an
allow-list of literal URL path characters, then encode them.

Every id these endpoints really see passes unchanged: a UUID, a Mongo id, a slug such as org-1,
and the literal "undefined" the invite page has always sent for an absent workspace.

Alerts 302, 303 (js/request-forgery).

fix(frontend): keep annotation grouping keys out of Object.prototype

reached the result anyway, because Object.entries does not enumerate it, so the guard drops

feat(runner): map proxy budget refusals to a clear starter-credits message

A run funded by starter credits routes through a budgeted model proxy. When the
organization's allowance is spent, the proxy refuses at admission with a 429 whose
body names the key and its spend. The condenser had no branch for it, so the raw
provider JSON reached the chat — the user saw a key fragment and a cost figure, and
no way to read "you are out of credits, add your own key".

Classify these refusals on the BODY, never on the status alone: 429 covers budget
refusals, per-key throttling, and upstream provider quota alike, and telling a user
their credits are gone when they were merely throttled is worse than saying nothing.

`conciseError` now returns the message half of `classifyRunError`, which also yields
a stable code the error event carries to the client. Copy is placeholder.

fix(runner): pin the live budget refusal, and stop retry chatter from hiding it

Live QA on the dev stack surfaced the exact frame a spent funded key produces, and
two things about it that the mapping alone did not cover.

The refusal arrives status-prefixed onto a bare body (not `{"error": {...}}`-wrapped),
and names the key twice: `Key=` is the organization UUID that aliases it, and the
parenthesized token is the key's suffix. Both are pinned as a fixture and asserted
absent from the mapped message, along with the spend figures.

The bigger one: pi-acp renders Pi's auto-retry events as assistant message chunks, so
a retried refusal leaves `run.output()` holding "Retrying (attempt 1/3, waiting 2s)..."
and nothing else. The swallowed-error recovery is guarded on an empty output, so it was
skipped and the turn shipped that chatter as its answer — the mapped message never had
a chance to fire. A turn holding only retry notices now counts as the empty turn it is.
