default, 80px on /m - so "scrolled up a little" meant something different on
every surface. They now share one rule in @agenta/chat: reveal at
max(200px, half a viewport) past the newest turn. Follow keeps its own tight
threshold, because auto-scrolling someone who scrolled up to read is the worse
failure.

The measurement takes the newest message id, because Virtuoso windows its rows:
on a settled thread scrolled far up the newest turn is not rendered, and
measuring the last rendered one would hide the pill exactly when it is needed.

Also adds jumpGateOpen, which suppresses the pill while a blocking HITL gate is
docked - they share the same bottom corner, and a paused run has nothing
arriving below to jump to. Its call sites are still uncommitted: they depend on
feat/connect-tools-dock and redesign/agent-approval-card.

fix(frontend): drop the dead band between transcript and composer

A 12px flex gap on the transcript column parked bare canvas between the
transcript and the composer. The transcript's bottom fade is meant to dissolve
content into the composer edge, so the fade ended on nothing and read as the
transcript being cut short.

Nothing depended on it: the column's in-flow children are the transcript, the
queue strip and the composer region, and every docked card already carries its
own mb-2.

fix(frontend): revive the jump pill, and polish the chat chrome

The jump-to-latest pill could stop appearing for good. `scheduleShowJump`
guarded its rAF with `if (handle) return`, and only the frame itself cleared
the handle - a hidden tab never runs rAF, so one backgrounded moment latched
the handle non-zero and killed every later measurement for the life of the
mount. Observed live: the pill stayed hidden at any distance, across reloads.
Both engines now cancel-and-reschedule (still one queued frame), and a
visibilitychange re-measure covers a tab brought back with no further
scrolling.

The pill also went see-through on hover in dark mode: the outline variant
hovers to --btn-default-hover-bg, which is rgba(255,255,255,0.04) there, so it
replaced the opaque background and streamed text read through it. It now holds
its background and shows hover through the border and text colour. Text drops
to 12px with a 14px arrow.

Collapsing a long message popped rather than eased, because mask-image cannot
be transitioned and the fade vanished the instant the toggle was clicked. The
mask now stays mounted and its SIZE animates - the gradient stretches to 4x the
box so only its opaque head remains - which dissolves the fade in step with the
height.

style(frontend): tighten the user bubble on both surfaces

The user turn inherited the antd-x metrics it was ported from - a 12px radius
with 16/12 padding - which left a one-line message swimming in its own box.
Now an 8px radius with 12/8 padding.

The geometry is one exported class in @agenta/ui so the desktop transcript and
/m cannot drift. Geometry only: the accent tint stays on the desktop, because
--ag-user-bubble-bg / --ag-user-bubble-border are defined in agenta-ui's
stylesheet and are not bridged into /m's generated tokens - pushing the tinted
class there would paint a transparent border on a transparent fill.

fix(frontend): keep the Virtuoso jump pill fresh, and trim comments

Review follow-up.

The Virtuoso engine measured the pill only from its scroll listener, so a
streaming Footer or messages arriving while the tab was hidden left showJump
stale with no scroll to correct it. The measurement is now a stable callback
backed by a scroller ref, driven by the scroll listener plus the same
[messages, status] and visibilitychange re-measures the plain engine already
had. Its rAF handle is also cancelled on unmount.

Condensed the comment blocks flagged against the repo's one-line guideline.

fix(frontend): resolve the review findings on the streamed-text reveal

- advanceByGraphemes returned from+1 when one cluster was longer than the
  segmentation window, splitting a surrogate pair and painting U+FFFD (an
  emoji carrying combining marks reproduces it). Grow the window until a
  complete cluster is in view instead.
- Cap reveals at ~30/s. Every reveal costs a markdown re-parse, and a Shiki
  re-highlight inside a fence, so revealing on every vsync tripled that work
  against the old 50ms commit for no perceptual gain.
- The client trace measured gaps across turn boundaries, so a user's think
  time between turns entered the histogram and wrecked the p90 the probe
  exists to report. Stamp each entry with its turn and skip the crossing pair.
- Make that trace opt-in like its runner half, and give it a real ring: it ran
  for every user and shift() re-indexed 2000 entries per delta once full.
- Move StreamingMarkdown out of the markdown module _app.tsx imports, so the
  @agenta/chat/hooks barrel stays out of the app shell's graph.
- Mobile ran the reveal loop on collapsed reasoning folds, pacing text that is
  never in the DOM.

fix(frontend): stop session tabs opening themselves

The playground tab strip grew on its own — one tab per automation or cron
run, forever. Nobody opened them.

`currentOpenIds` treated "this scope has no open list yet" as "every session
in history is open". That fallback existed to carry pre-`:v2` sessions across
the rekey, but those keys are hard-deleted at module load, so it had nothing
left to migrate. What it did instead was hand the strip everything the
reconciler adopts — and that query has no origin filter and includes ended and
archived runs, so every background run for the agent became a tab. Reconcile
never writes the open list, so a scope in the fallback never left it.

The open list is now the only thing that opens a tab.

A scope could also stay in the fallback permanently. The seed effect latched
`seeded` before calling `addSession`, and the session store silently drops
writes made before a project resolves — so an early seed latched against a
session that was never stored, and the latch only re-arms while the list is
empty, which the reconciler ends by filling history. Seeding now waits for the
project.

fix(frontend): stop a refetch handing back the name a rename just replaced

Renaming a session the playground has open wrote the new title locally and
fired the header write, then patched every cached list that renders a name. One
cache it never patched was internal-reconciliation — the per-agent server list
the chat panel folds into its tab cache, taking the REMOTE title over the local
one. So the next refetch of it, on focus or on its own minute tick, handed the
old name straight back.

Patch that cache with the others, and await the local rename the way archive and
delete now do: renameSessionAtomFamily returns its header write for exactly this
reason, and the seam it crossed dropped it.

chore(frontend): drop the sidebar code nothing reaches

Four leftovers, none of them wired to anything: an oss SessionRowActions the
row wrapper stopped importing when the shared one landed, a sessionOptions
module only its own test still names, two entity definitions that never shipped
and sat commented out, and groupingStartsFolded — a function taking a grouping
and answering false for all of them, which made collapsedKeys' XOR against it
just a set membership test.

The test-set and evaluator KEYS stay: their static rows still use them.

fix(frontend): take archived agents out of the agent list

agentWorkflowsListQueryStateAtom filtered on is_agent alone, while the prompts
list beside it filters deleted_at too — same rows, same field, one of them
applied. So an archived agent kept its place in the rail and, worse, stayed an
option in the sessions filter's Agent facet, where picking it emptied a list it
could no longer fill: dropArchivedAgentSessions had already taken its sessions
off the rail (#5944). Nothing offered a way back out of that filter either,
since the option stops being listed once you clear it.

fix(frontend): give a truncated rail row something to hover

getTooltip was plumbed the whole way — entity config, registry, row model, and
two test files — and no entity set one. It would not have shown if they had:
NavMenu renders item.tooltip only on the collapsed icon rail, and both list
groups hide their children there. Meanwhile a row carried no title attribute at
all, so "Daily learning snipp…" had no hover text anywhere.

The label now carries its own: the entity's tooltip where there is one, the full
title otherwise. Sessions supplies the one the seam was built for (#5945) — the
owning agent, which the label cannot say and the heading only says under agent
grouping.

feat(frontend): order the desktop agent rail by most recently used

Catalog order reads as random once you have more than a handful of agents. The
mobile rail has ranked them by last session since it shipped, off ranks derived
from the sessions the rail already holds — no extra request — while the desktop
rail rendered whatever order the catalog returned.

Rather than special-case agents in the source aggregator, entities name a ranks
atom and the registry applies withRefsByRecency to any that does. Sessions is
alwaysOpen on desktop, so reading its refs for the ranks subscribes nothing that
was not subscribed already.

fix(frontend): gate the agent ranks on the Sessions group, like the facet beside it

The ranks map is the Agents group reading the SESSIONS list, and it read them
ungated — so a rail whose Sessions group is closed kept those queries subscribed
and polling, which is the fetching that group's own gate exists to stop. Desktop
acquired it with the recency ordering; mobile has had it since the drawer's
ranks landed, bounded only by the sheet unmounting.

The open-state test the agent facet already ran is now shared by both readers, so
neither host can drift from it. Empty ranks mean catalog order, which is what an
unopened Sessions group could tell you anyway.

fix(frontend): rank the agent rail off an unfiltered query, not the filtered list

Filtering sessions reordered the Agents group. The rank map was derived from the
rail's own session list, which carries every filter — so narrowing to one agent
left only that agent with a timestamp and dropped the rest to catalog order, and
a status or activity filter reshuffled them the same way. A filter is not a use.

Ranks now come from their own project-scoped, origin-agnostic query with no
activity floor, so an agent's rank is its true last activity and a session filter
cannot touch it. Low-priority, un-polled, and gated on the Sessions group like
the facet beside it, so a closed rail fetches nothing. One shared atom, so the
fix reaches desktop and mobile together.

fix(frontend): cancel the run when its session tab is closed

Close a tab mid-run and the session came back stuck: reopening it showed the
running-elsewhere strip, and the transcript sat behind a 15s-to-60s catch-up
poll that had nothing new to adopt.

Closing only unmounts the pane, and the pane's teardown calls `stop()` — the
client-side abort. That ends this browser's fetch and nothing else. The runner
keeps going and keeps the session's alive lock, so the liveness poll keeps
reporting it as running long after the tab is gone.

Closing a running tab now sends the same cooperative cancel the Stop button
does, so the backend releases the lock at the moment the user walks away.

`awaiting` is deliberately left alone: a parked approval is durable and meant
to be answered later, so closing its tab must not throw the turn away. The
rule is a pure function so that carve-out stays pinned by a test.

feat(frontend): close other session tabs, or the ones to the right

The tab strip had one close affordance: the × on a single tab. Clearing a
strip that had grown long meant clicking × over and over.

A tab's context menu now carries Chrome's bulk closes — Close, Close other
tabs, Close tabs to the right — each disabled when it would do nothing.

Pinned tabs survive "close other tabs", as they do in a browser. Since pins
lead the strip they are never to the right of anything, so the carve-out only
shows up in that one verb.

The strip computes the ids because "to the right" means the RENDERED order,
which is pin-sorted and only the strip knows. `closeSessionsAtomFamily` then
applies the whole set in one write, with the same rules a single close has:
sessions stay in history and stay reopenable, never-run husks are discarded,
and the active tab moves to the nearest survivor. Closing a running tab still
cancels its run.

fix(frontend): give an open session an activity date in the rail

A session open in the playground reaches the rail as a host-local ref, and those
refs carried no activityAt — so under date grouping every one of them fell into
the "No activity" heading, the date bucket for a row with no timestamp. Set it
from the session's own lastMessageAt, then createdAt, the same key the history
picker orders by.

fix(frontend): give status grouping an Awaiting input bucket

Grouping by status had only Running, Live and Idle, while the status FILTER
offers Awaiting input — so a session waiting on you landed under Idle, its amber
dot contradicting the heading. Add the bucket, ranked above liveness the way the
gate outranks it everywhere else: Running, Awaiting input, Live, Idle.

feat(frontend): give the agent filter an All agents row, selected by default

The Agent facet already treats an empty set as every agent, but the only way
back to that from the menu was deselecting each agent one at a time. Add an All
agents row that clears the set, checked whenever nothing is selected — so it is
the default state and a single click returns to it.

The checked-when-empty behaviour is a small FilterMenu primitive (noneValue), so
any multi-choice facet can offer the same way back to all.

fix(frontend): don't jump the selection to the agent when a session's group collapses

Grouped by agent, a selected session sits under its agent's heading. Collapsing
that heading drops the session row from the rendered tree, so its pinned key no
longer resolved and the selection fell through to the route match — which is the
AGENT row, since a session's row links to its agent's playground. Collapsing a
group thus moved the highlight onto the agent, falsely saying you were viewing it.

A pinned key naming an unrendered row now selects nothing rather than the route
match, whether the row was collapsed away or filtered out. Extracted the decision
as resolveSelectedKey so the three cases are explicit.

fix(frontend): pin the mobile session so a collapse doesn't move its highlight

Mobile's session route is unique (`/sessions/<id>`), so route matching highlights
the open session on its own — until its agent heading is collapsed, when the row
leaves the tree and the `/sessions` parent prefix-matches the route and grabs the
highlight.

Mobile now pins the open session from its route, the same key the row carries, so
selection flows through the shared `resolveSelectedKey`: the session while its row
renders, nothing once a collapse hides it. Same behaviour desktop got, through the
same package helper — mobile just sources the id from the route instead of a tab
cache.

fix(frontend): stop re-reading a session's whole record log on every connect

Reopening a long session was slow, and got slow again every time you came
back to the tab.

The watch relay emits `ready` on every connect, and the relay connects on each
tab activation and each return to a foreground window. `ready` was wired to the
same handler as `records-changed`, so each of those invalidated the records
query and re-read the entire log — a ~200KB fetch at `priority: "low"`, a full
remap, and a `setMessages` that replaces the transcript and re-renders every
row. On reopen that ran right beside the mount's own revalidation, so the log
was read twice within a second.

`ready` now has its own handler that skips a read the mount is already doing,
or one that finished within the relay's own coalescing window.

The skip is safe because of what `ready` is for. A change can land after the
response headers flush but before the Redis subscribe completes, reaching
neither the stream nor a revalidation driven by `onopen` — `ready` closes that
window. A read of the log newer than the connection cannot have missed such a
change, so repeating it buys nothing. A change after the subscribe arrives as
`records-changed`, which is never skipped; that is why the two events needed
separating rather than sharing a deduped handler.

Every full read now reports itself, so "nobody has read this" and "a read is
running right now" are distinguishable — the second is the reopen case, where
the mount's revalidation is still in flight when `ready` lands.

feat(frontend): mark automation sessions with a bolt in the rail

Chats and automation runs looked identical in the rail — same dot, no way to tell
which was which. The row now carries isAutomation (from the immutable trigger
origin, a base field so no wider fetch), and the glyph says the type: a bolt for a
trigger run, the dot for a chat. Chatting inside an automation does not change its
origin, so it stays a bolt — which is the truth, it is still that run.

State still wins the glyph: a live turn spins and a gate paints it amber for both
types, so distinguishing the type never costs the running or waiting signal. Both
hosts, off one shared ref field.

chore(frontend): tighten two doc comments per review

CodeRabbit flagged the ranksAtom and renameCache comments against the repo's
one-line-comment rule. Collapse the ranksAtom note to one line; trim the
renameCache note while keeping the constraint it documents.

fix(frontend): repair the CI gates the branch broke

Three compile/format failures CI caught that lint did not:

- mobileNavScope dropped its @agenta/navigation-ui import when useRouter was
  added, so the header/footer slots lost SidebarLogo/Banners/ToggleButton.
- SessionRail still called isSessionHusk with the old (session, messages)
  signature after it became (session, hasMessages); pass the per-session
  boolean through sessionHasMessages.
- A stray blank line in the sidebar test failed the prettier gate.

fix(frontend): keep the template strip header intact at narrow widths

The header was one flex row with no shrink control, so the category tabs
overflowed and squeezed the pager: the counter wrapped to two lines and the
arrow buttons were compressed out of square. The tabs now take the leftover
width and scroll inside it (masked at the overflow edge), and the label,
counter, and button cluster hold their size.

The arrow and menu buttons move to the shared @agenta/ui small icon button,
so they size and disable like every other control instead of hand-rolled
chrome.
chore(frontend): tighten two doc comments per review

fix(frontend): a backdrop click closes the drawer again

`EnhancedDrawer` read `closeOnLayoutClick` as "suppress outside-click
dismissal" (`closeOnLayoutClick ?? maskClosable`), which inverted the prop's
antd-era meaning and left the ~18 drawers that pass `closeOnLayoutClick={false}`
closable only via the X.

Under the antd wrapper the prop was ADDITIVE, not a switch: a `document` click
listener that ALSO closed the drawer when the click landed inside `.ant-layout`
(for maskless drawers, where no mask catches the click), skipping
`.variant-table-row`. The mask kept dismissing on a backdrop click regardless,
because antd's `maskClosable` defaults to `true` — so in production every one of
those drawers did close on an outside click.

`maskClosable` alone governs dismissal now, exactly as in antd.
`closeOnLayoutClick` stays on the prop surface (no call-site churn) and is inert:
Radix's dismissable layer already closes on any outside pointerdown, a superset
of the old `.ant-layout` listener. A drawer that genuinely must not dismiss on a
backdrop click says `maskClosable={false}` — the one call-site with that written
intent (AgentIntegrationDrawer) has its docstring corrected rather than its
behaviour changed, since it never held under antd either.

`EnhancedModal` was never affected — it has no `closeOnLayoutClick` and reads
`maskClosable` directly — but the outside-click suite covers it too so the answer
stays true.

fix(frontend): switch organizations, not workspaces, in the mobile switcher

Every organization's default workspace is named "Default", so the /m drawer's
second panel rendered one indistinguishable "Default" row per org. A multi-org
account had no way to tell them apart, which read as "the organization does not
switch on mobile" — the trigger already named the org, only the list did not.

Group by organization instead (groupByOrganization), label rows with the org
name, and say "Switch organization" like the desktop rail. The workspace stays
in the URL: each project row now routes with its OWN workspace id, so an org
with several workspaces switches correctly too.

Fixes #6228

fix(frontend): hide demo projects on mobile, as the desktop already does

The desktop hides demo projects everywhere (projectsAtom) and prefers a
non-demo project post-login. /m applied neither, so an account with a demo org
could sign in on a phone and be resolved straight into a demo project the
desktop never offers, with the demo org sitting in the switcher next to the
real ones.

Move filterOutDemoProjects into @agenta/entities/project — one implementation
both shells share, rather than a second copy — and apply it at /m's fetch
boundary, so the context resolver, the switcher, and post-sign-in landing all
agree with the desktop.

Refs #6228

fix(frontend): resolve mobile group labels from the whole group

Review catch: an organization whose FIRST project row carried no name kept the
fallback label even when a later row supplied the real one. Reproduced in a
test, along with a second case the same shape — a blank name ("") slipped past
`??` and rendered an empty switcher row.

Both come from one habit: group-level fields were read off whichever row
happened to arrive first. Restructure so grouping buckets the rows first, then
resolves every group field across the WHOLE bucket. Names go through a
firstNonBlank helper, so blank is treated as missing rather than as a name.

Along the way:
- RoutableProject makes "has a workspace, so it can be routed to" a type, not a
  guard repeated per grouper. Project rows no longer need a workspace_id
  fallback at the call site.
- OrganizationGroup.key is now separate from organizationId, which stays null
  for a workspace-keyed row instead of holding a synthetic "workspace:<id>".
- OrganizationGroup.workspaceId comes from the group's first project, so the
  workspace an org row enters cannot disagree with the project it lands on.
- WorkspaceGroup drops workspaceName and organizationName. Nothing reads them
  since the switcher moved to groupByOrganization, and leaving display fields on
  a routing-only type is what invited the first-row bug.

chore(frontend): trim the comments added to the mobile switcher

web/CLAUDE.md caps in-code comments at one short line. The blocks added in the
previous two commits narrated rationale in prose instead. Cut to one line each,
keeping only the constraints that are not visible in the code.

Leaves the two pre-existing comments in DrawerProjectSwitcher alone. They are
untouched by this PR and rewriting them here would be unrelated diff noise.

refactor(frontend): drop the inert closeOnLayoutClick prop

Follow-up to the backdrop-dismissal fix. `closeOnLayoutClick` no longer does
anything: `maskClosable` alone governs outside-click dismissal, and Radix's
dismissable layer already covers what the old `.ant-layout` click listener added.
Leaving a silent no-op on the prop surface invites the next reader to believe it
suppresses dismissal — which is exactly how the drawers ended up closable only
via the X.

Removed from the facade's props, from the `GenericDrawer` / `AnnotateDrawer` /
`TestcaseDrawer` type surfaces, and from all 19 call-sites. `maskClosable={false}`
is now the single, explicit opt-out for a drawer that must not dismiss on a
backdrop click; no drawer takes it yet, so every one of them closes on an outside
click as it did under antd.

Five call-sites carried a comment claiming an outside click could not drop their
draft or setup (TemplateSetupDrawer, ConfigItemDrawer, InstructionsDrawer,
SectionDrawer, AgentIntegrationDrawer). That was never true under antd either, so
the comments go rather than the behaviour — those are the five to revisit first if
the team wants the opt-in.

fix(frontend): give the rail kebab a themed focus ring, not the UA blue

Closing the row's kebab menu left a stray blue box on the trigger: Radix returns

[AGE-4197] fix(frontend): lay the drawer rail out against dvh, paint it against the sheet

The nav drawer mounts the shared SidebarShell inside a sheet, and the rail sized
itself with `100vh`. On a phone browser `vh` is the toolbars-HIDDEN height, so
with the toolbar showing the rail ran past the bottom of the screen and its last
rows — Settings, Help & Docs, and the project/org switcher — sat underneath it,
with nothing to scroll to reach them. The switcher is the only way to change
project or organization on `/m`, so it read as missing entirely. Hiding Safari's
toolbar brought it back, which is the tell.

Splitting the two jobs the one height was doing:

- The SURFACE (`aside`) fills the sheet, so it still bleeds behind the toolbar.
  Sizing it to `dvh` instead fixes the bug but leaves a strip of page showing
  through beneath the drawer, which reads as a rendering fault.
- The CONTENT column measures `var(--ag-viewport-height, 100dvh)`: `dvh` tracks
  the visible viewport as the toolbars come and go, and the variable narrows it
  again while a soft keyboard is open — the same expression AppShell,
  ScreenScaffold and SessionWorkspace already use.

The bottom block reserves `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`, since the home
indicator sits inside `dvh`.

The docked rail keeps its sticky `100vh` geometry: it lives in a
document-scrolling page, where a height that changed with the toolbars would
reflow the sidebar mid-scroll.

`onDismiss` already distinguishes the two mounts — the resizer keys off it for
the same reason — so no new prop.

fix(frontend): declutter the instructions drawer and gate its Save on a real edit

looked like an edit. Track the content the drawer opened with and gate Save on a
real diff against it, the way the section drawers already do. This rides on a
new `dirty` prop rather than `disabled`, which also drives the editor and chips.

fix(frontend): polish the skill config drawer and its editors

Strips the skill drawer's header chrome (icon, type badge, subtitle, footer
note) so the form carries the identity, moves the behaviour flags under an

feat(frontend): dock the agent question form above the composer

The request_input form rendered as one inline transcript card holding every
field at once. It grew and shrank as you typed, and each height change drove
the transcript's ResizeObserver into a scroll write, so the composer moved

Replace it with a fixed-height card pinned above the composer, beside the

because the keys mean different things in each:

[AGE-4197] fix(frontend): let the mobile drawer meet the top of the screen

iOS composites the status-bar strip from the page's top colour, and the strip sits
directly above the nav drawer. With a dimmed scrim over a light page that strip
rendered mid-grey against a near-white drawer, reading as the drawer stopping
short of the screen rather than as browser chrome. It is not a safe-area inset:
`safe-area-inset-top` measures 0 in a Safari tab, `theme-color` does not override
the strip, and a full-bleed drawer does not change it either — all three were
tried on an iPhone 17 / iOS 26.1 before landing here.

What does move it is the colour the strip composites from:

- `body` paints the rail's surface rather than the page's, so the strip lands on
  the drawer's own colour.
- The scrim is clear below `lg`, since any alpha darkens that strip. Above `lg`
  there is no strip to tint and the dim stays.
- Each sheet casts a shadow away from its anchored edge below `lg`, carrying the
  separation the scrim used to.

which is an antd modal — `/m` ships no antd, so it arrived unthemed and laid out
badly over a keyboard. `CreateProjectSheet` is the app's own `side="responsive"`

fix(frontend): stop the mobile picker losing an early colour pick

Three review findings, all in the mobile sheet.

- A colour tapped before the lazily-loaded catalog arrived was committed with an empty
  path. The record guard rejects a path that is not markup, so the write persisted and
  then read back as null: the pick vanished, silently, and re-tapping repeated it. The
  sheet now shows nothing pickable until the catalog lands, so an empty path cannot be
  committed at all.
- The seed loader swallowed a failed chunk (its rejection handler returned undefined),
  leaving a blank chip and no way to tell a failure from a slow load. There is now one
  loader for the whole sheet, so the header and the grid cannot disagree about whether it
  arrived, and one error state with a retry.
- The OS colour input fires on every drag frame, so one gesture was dozens of localStorage
  writes, each re-serialising the whole map. It previews live and commits on a trailing
  delay, which is what the desktop picker does with its drag.

second loader. The conic-gradient swatch moves into colors.ts as AGENT_ICON_CONIC, and the

feat(frontend): give the question card a picker, a check mark and a chip field

Every card in this file shares one toolCallId, so the stepper restored the

fix(frontend): close six gaps a review found in the question card

The Other row on a multi-select wrote its text straight into the value, which
dropped every picked option and put a string on a wire the schema declared as an
array. It now contributes one more entry beside them.

A skipped step was validated again by the primary action, so a one-question
required form could never finish: its skip has no next step to move to and the

fix(frontend): address the review findings on the agent icon

From the CodeRabbit pass on #6351.

- Validate a stored glyph element by element instead of trusting it to start with a
  bracket. The path reaches dangerouslySetInnerHTML, and localStorage is outside the trust
  boundary, so a hand-edited entry could previously carry any markup. Only the shapes the
  generator emits are accepted now. Checked against all 160 catalog icons.

  atom as null, and reading a key off it threw.

fix(frontend): take the regexes out of the two checks CodeQL flagged

The screen that rejected catastrophic schema patterns was itself polynomial on a
crafted pattern, which is the same bug one level up. It scans the pattern by hand
now, tracking group depth and whether a group held a quantifier, so it catches
(a+)+ and (a{2,})+ without running a regex of its own.

The email check had two adjacent greedy runs either side of a literal dot, which
backtracks on an address like a@ followed by many "!.". It is index arithmetic
now: one @ with something either side, and a dot inside the domain.

refactor(frontend): keep @agenta/navigation headless

CI lint caught the layering: @agenta/navigation is headless by rule, and importing
@agenta/entity-ui to render an agent glyph in the sidebar registry broke it. I checked for
a dependency cycle when I added it and found none, but missed that the constraint is
explicit and lint-enforced.

`rowIcons` seam beside the `kindIcon` and `rowWrappers` it already takes, and the oss
sidebar supplies the agent glyph through it. The package only calls what the app hands it.

style(frontend): order the sidebar hook imports for the oss config

fix(frontend): read a pattern's character classes, and clamp a shrunk draft

Inside a character class `+`, `*` and `{` are literals, so the catastrophic-shape
scanner read `(a[+])+` as a nested quantifier and quietly stopped enforcing a
pattern that was fine.

A draft also clamped its index to the number of steps rather than to the last
screen. A five-question draft restored against a re-asked one-question schema
landed past its only step, which renders neither the question nor a review while
the primary action completes. Both are covered by tests that fail without them.

fix(frontend): allowlist SVG attributes and give the glyph a real contrast floor

Three review findings on the icon record and the colour maths.

The stored-path guard checked element names but let any attribute through, so
a hand-edited localStorage entry could carry <path onload=...> into
dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Attributes are now parsed and matched against a
geometry/presentation allowlist; all 160 catalog icons still pass.

readableInk used a perceived-lightness threshold, which passes mid-greys that
are unreadable in practice: #A9A9A9 landed at 2.16:1 on its own tint. It now
darkens until the glyph clears WCAG 3:1 against that tint. One palette colour
moves as a result, amber #CA8A04 (2.67:1) to #B67C04.

The mobile swatch row kept a queued custom-colour commit alive across a Reset,
so the record could reappear 150ms after being cleared. The row now cancels the
pending commit when the selection goes back to null.

fix(frontend): keep a long option list's cursor on screen

The list caps at 220px and scrolls, so past the sixth row an arrow key moved a
cursor the user could no longer see. The cursor row now scrolls itself into view

fix(frontend): move the chip field's commit key out of its placeholder

Inside the placeholder the arrow read as part of the prompt. It now sits at the
field's trailing edge, where the option rows already put theirs, so the
placeholder is just "Add one". Suppressed on touch, which has no such key.

fix(frontend): undim the question number

It sits beside the label it belongs to, so a tertiary tone read as chrome rather
than as part of the question. Matches the option rows, whose index is already
full strength.

fix(frontend): make an option row's cursor as visible as its selection

Quaternary fill was too faint to show which row the pointer or the arrow keys
were on. The cursor now takes the same fill a picked row has; the bold label and
the trailing check are what still tell a selection apart.

fix(frontend): stop a long date hint overflowing its trigger

The picker used the schema's description as its placeholder, so a sentence-length
hint ran past the trigger's edge and repeated the question line word for word.
The placeholder is generic now, and the trigger truncates as a backstop.

fix(frontend): print a step's hint once, on the question line

Text, number and multiline fields also carried the schema description as their
placeholder, so every hint appeared twice and a sentence-length one ran past the
field's edge. The question line keeps it; the multiline field keeps only the

fix(frontend): spell the newline shortcut, and let Skip drop its border

"Shift ↵" leaned on the Apple glyph for a key most keyboards label Enter. It now
reads "Shift + Enter", matching the composer, which spells Enter as a word on
every platform and branches only for the modifier that genuinely differs.

fix(frontend): give the long-answer field the composer's newline key

Enter and Cmd/Ctrl+Enter both moved to the next question, so the card spent two
keys on one job and left the newline on Shift, which the composer never teaches.
The modifier now breaks the line in the multiline field, exactly as it does in
the composer, and the caret is restored after the value round-trips.

Everywhere else it still fires the primary action: on a multi-select and on the
review list it is the only way forward, since Enter toggles a row there.

fix(frontend): stop a long option list squashing its own rows

The rows are flex children of a column with a max height, so once a step had
more options than the cap could hold, flex shrank every row instead of scrolling
the list. The more choices a question offered, the thinner each one got: eight
options rendered at 26px against a declared 30px. They hold their height now and
the list scrolls, which is what the cap was there for.

fix(frontend): match the question card's eyebrow to the approval card's

Same icon size and the same gap beside it. The two docks stack in the composer
region, so a pixel of difference between their headers reads as a mistake rather
than as a distinction.

fix(frontend): open an option's tooltip beside it, not over the list

The default placement covered the rows above, hiding the choices the reader is
comparing this one against at the moment they ask what it means.

fix(frontend): mark an option's explanation with an info icon

A question mark meant two things in one card: the eyebrow's, which says this is a
request for input, and the row's, which explains a choice. The row takes the info
glyph, so the two stop competing.

feat(website): serve markdown, JSON errors, and an OpenAPI spec to agents

An agent-readiness audit scored agenta.ai 61/100: no content negotiation, no
Vary, no structured errors, no published API spec, and a 404 an agent cannot
recover from. None of that is expressible in pure static assets, so add a thin
worker in front of the Cloudflare assets binding. Astro stays output:'static' —
the worker never renders, it picks between prebuilt files and sets headers.

- worker/: Accept negotiation with q-values, Vary: Accept, 406 for types we
  cannot serve, a markdown or JSON 404 depending on who is asking, and the
  _headers /* policy re-applied (Cloudflare drops _headers on worker
  responses). The whole handler falls back to the raw asset on any throw.
- src/pages/*.md.ts: a prebuilt markdown twin of every route, blog bodies
  rendered from their own MDX with the JSX stripped. This is also the real fix
  for 'content without JavaScript'.
- scripts/copy-openapi.mjs: publishes /openapi.json at build from the committed
  docs spec, rewriting the relative /api server to the us/eu cloud base URLs
  and dropping the admin surface.

Two routing decisions matter and are easy to get wrong: run_worker_first is an
allowlist of HTML routes (a blanket /* would kill the four _redirects 308s and
the image cache policy), and not_found_handling is 'none' (with '404-page' the
asset server answers unknown paths itself and no agent ever reaches the worker).

Browsers, crawlers, and bare curl keep the designed 404 page and the identical
HTML. Covered by vitest, a postbuild output check, and a post-deploy smoke test
both workflows now run.

body does — so the X-Robots-Tag the twin endpoints set was never served. A
crawler following the rel=alternate link in Base.astro would have indexed

asset, so it lives there now, and the deploy smoke test asserts both halves:
the twin is noindex, the HTML page is not.

fix(website): rank every acceptable representation, not just the best one

Review of #6361 surfaced two symptoms of one flaw: the worker picked a single
winner from the Accept header and then ignored what else the client would have
taken. A request for "application/json, text/markdown" got HTML it never asked
for, and "Accept: text/html;q=0" (an explicit refusal) was read as no
preference and answered with HTML anyway.

acceptedRepresentations now returns the ranked list of representations the
client accepts, and the worker walks it: markdown when it outranks HTML, the
page when HTML is acceptable, 406 when neither is. A path that does not exist
still gets its 404 first — a missing page owes a 404 in the caller's language,
not a 406 about representations of nothing.

Also from the review:

- copy-openapi rejects a spec with no info.title/version. It would have
  published a file that parses and tells a client nothing.
- mdxToMarkdown protects inline code spans, so a post that mentions
  `<InlineCTA />` in a sentence keeps the example instead of losing it.
- The scroll-layout beat title goes back to a span. It sits inside a
  role="button" row, where a heading is exposed as presentational, so it bought
  nothing; the no-JS layout that crawlers actually receive keeps its real h3.
- /llms.txt says the homepage twin is /index.md. Appending .md to "/" yields
  /.md, which is not a route.
- The deploy smoke test asserts the text/html media type rather than one exact
  header serialization (production omits the charset, so all three post-deploy
  checks failed), and skips the indexable-page assertion on workers.dev, which
  Cloudflare stamps noindex by default.

fix(website): resolve each representation against its most specific Accept range

Second review round on #6361. Three correctness holes, all in how the edge
worker and the MDX converter handle input they were scanning too loosely.

A specific q=0 now overrides a wildcard that accepted the same type. The old
forward scan read "text/*;q=1, text/html;q=0" as accepting HTML, because the
exact range only excluded itself. Each representation is now resolved against
the most specific range that matches it, per RFC 9110 12.5.1, so that header
yields markdown only.

A request that accepts nothing we serve gets a 406 even when the path does not
exist. There is no language to answer the 404 in, so 406 is the honest reply.

mdxToMarkdown protects every code region markdown allows, not just triple
backticks: tilde fences and any run of backticks are pulled out before the
component cleanup. The placeholder is wrapped in NUL bytes, so a post whose
prose happens to read "CODE0" is no longer corrupted on the way back in.

Declined one comment on the thread: application/xhtml+xml and application/xml
still map to the HTML page. Those clients read it fine, and a 406 is a worse
answer than a content type one notch broader than the request.

[feat] Split the agent Tools section into Integrations and Subagents (#6375)

* feat(playground): split the agent Tools section into Integrations and Subagents

The agent config panel had one Tools section whose body carried four sub-headers:
Integrations, Workflow references, Tool definitions and Built-in. The section header's
plus opened a four-item dropdown that spanned all of them.

"Tools" stops working as a name once subagents become their own section, because a
subagent is also a tool: a Tools header sitting next to a Subagents header claims the two
are different kinds of thing when one contains the other. So the section is now called
Integrations and holds only connected apps, and the referenced workflows move up into a
Subagents section of their own.

Each section now has exactly one add action, so both plus buttons open their drawer
directly and the dropdown is gone. AgentToolSelectorPopover had no other caller, so it and
its story go with it.

Tool definitions and provider built-ins are no longer rendered, because tool definitions
are being removed as a feature. An older config may still carry either kind. Those entries
stay in the saved config and still run, but this panel neither lists nor edits them.

Nothing on the wire changes. A subagent is still saved as {type: "reference"} inside the
same flat tools array, and both sections share the tools draft and validation indicator
key, so the section-diff machinery is untouched.

* feat(playground): redesign the add-subagent drawer, and give Subagents a robot icon

The old surface was a two-panel master/detail drawer. It made the author choose one workflow,
then pin a version or an environment, then read its resolved input schema before adding it.
Three things were wrong with it.

Authors add helpers in batches, so single-select was the wrong primitive. This is a
checkable list. The whole card toggles, select-all acts on whatever the search is showing,
and agents already added are listed for context but cannot be picked twice.

Of everything the detail panel showed, only the description ever decided the choice. The
card now carries the five fields that answer "what does this one do and what can it reach":
the agent's own icon, its name, its description, the model it runs on, and the apps it has
connected. Slug, version, revision and schema are gone. The model line draws the provider's
own mark, the same way the app line draws each integration's logo.

The words workflow and reference describe how the entry is saved, not what the author is
doing. Nothing on this surface says either one. The section icon is now a robot.

The component is presentational: every agent arrives as a prop, so the layout is storied
and can be iterated without the project's workflow queries. Six stories cover the default
list, a short list, no agents, loading, long content on every field, and all-already-added.
Story logos are inline data URIs rather than a public CDN, because a story that reaches the
network fails in CI and on a laptop with no egress.

NOT WIRED YET. The container still opens the old selector. Two of the five fields, the
model and the connected apps, are not on WorkflowReferenceUI today, so the bridge has to
grow before this can replace it.

* refactor(playground): share the row, the description and the logo run across the agent pickers

The add-subagent drawer had reinvented three things the codebase already had. This makes each
one a single implementation that every surface draws through, and rebuilds the drawer on them.

The row. The integration drawer settled the shape: a flat row divided by a hairline, a leading
mark, a title with a meta line under it, and the action on the right. That action is what adds,
and the same button removes afterwards, so the drawer's own footer only says Done. The subagent
drawer had grown a different model, a card with a checkbox that staged a selection for a footer
button to commit. It now uses the same row, and so do the integration drawer's own two rows,
through the new CatalogListRow. Bulk add moved to the section header, where a bulk action belongs.

The description. Long text looked bad because the subagent card clamped and stopped there. The
permission drawer already had the answer: clamp, measure while collapsed, and offer Show more only
when text is really hidden. That is now ExpandableDescription, which also carries the two rules
that were easy to miss, that a newline is always expandable and that no description means no
toggle. The permission drawer's tool rows and both integration rows now go through it, and the
catalog rows gained Show more they never had.

The logo run. Integrations have logos and the template cards already draw them well, as marks side
by side with the name on hover, instead of a logo-plus-name pair per app. That is now LogoMarks in
@agenta/ui, which is below both packages that need it. TemplateProviderMarks keeps its provider
lookup and delegates the drawing, so a template card and a subagent row cannot drift.

One behaviour changed outside the new drawer: an integration row in the All apps list can now
expand its description. Everything else is the same markup reached through a shared component.

* style(playground): apply the designer's pass to the add-subagent drawer

Taken from the designer's five artboards, read as inline styles rather than eyeballed.

The rows now sit in one bordered, rounded card instead of floating on the drawer ground. The
integration drawer already did this; the subagent drawer was the odd one out, so this is parity
rather than a new idea. Both list containers now use the same 6px radius.

The meta line gained a dot between the model and the connected apps. A gap alone let the two runs
read as one list of marks. The provider mark moved into a 13px tile the same size as an
integration logo, so the line reads as one run, and the model name is tabular so a column of
version digits does not look ragged.

Row padding goes to 10px vertical, the title line to a 24px minimum matching the small button
beside it, the icon chip to 28px, and the row divider to colorSplit, which is what a separator
inside a bordered list should be rather than a full border weight.

Two fixes came out of screenshotting rather than reading.

The loading state was a diagonal staircase of overlapping bars. Skeleton in @agenta/ui is the
antd COMPOSITE, an avatar plus a title plus three paragraph rows, so sizing it with a className
puts four bars in a box meant for one. Its own doc comment records four call sites that made this
mistake; this was the fifth. The skeleton now uses SkeletonBlock and carries the row's real
anatomy, including the trailing action, so the list does not jump when the agents land.

The long-content story now holds two rows with the same long description, so a reviewer can
expand one and read it against the collapsed one without hunting for a second story.

Not taken from the design: the drawer's close button stays on the left, because EnhancedDrawer
owns that and it is used across the app. The section header's count keeps its bordered tag rather
than becoming a filled pill, because SubSectionHeader has no story and one of its three call
sites lives in oss/src with no coverage, so the change could not be verified here.

* style(ui): match the logo marks to the drawer's 3px tiles

The designer's pass puts every small tile in a row on a 3px radius: the provider mark next to the
model, and each connected app's logo. LogoMarks was still on the 4px scale radius, so the run read
as slightly rounder than the tile beside it. The no-logo fallback also moves to the quaternary
fill, which is the ground the design uses for a tile carrying a letter rather than a mark.

This is shared with the template cards on the agent home page, where the marks render at 16px. A
2px radius change reads as nothing there, which is the point: one component, one look.

* fix(ui): drop an eslint disable for a rule this package does not load

CI's TypeScript lint job went red on the branch. @agenta/ui runs its own lint script from
inside the package, and the Next plugin does not match there, so the
"eslint-disable-next-line @next/next/no-img-element" I had added named a rule that is not
defined. ESLint treats that as an error in its own right: "Definition for rule ... was not
found". It passed locally only because I ran eslint from web/ against the file path, where a
different config block matched and the plugin was loaded.

The disable was never needed. TemplateProviderMarks carried the same plain img with no
disable before this branch, which is the precedent. The comment explaining why next/image is
wrong here stays, since that is the part a reader needs.

* chore(ui): reword a comment so no line starts with an eslint directive token

The replacement comment wrapped onto a line beginning with the eslint-disable token. ESLint
matches a directive on that leading token, so the sentence could have been read as a
file-wide suppression. A probe on this file was inconclusive, because the config reports
nothing there either way. Rewording costs nothing and removes the question.

* fix(playground): address the review of the Integrations and Subagents split

Six defects, all introduced by this branch, all found by an independent review and then
verified against the code before fixing.

The Subagents section never auto-expanded when its first subagent landed.
CONTROLLED_SECTION_KEYS did not list it, so the open-state and count entries the section
wrote were dead.

Integrations and Subagents shared one validation key, so an integration that needed
re-authentication put a warning on the Subagents header while every subagent row was clean.
The two sections now own their validation separately. They still share the CHANGE mark,
because both really do render out of the same `tools` schema field, and that is now stated
in one map rather than implied.

On a host with no gateway bridge, such as mobile, an empty Integrations section rendered a
focusable "add an integration" link wired to undefined. The section is now gated the same
way Subagents is, and the empty-state add is optional on both list bodies, so no dead
control is reachable.

Subagent rows were keyed by array position. Removing an earlier tool renumbers every row
below it, so React reused the wrong subtree. Rows are keyed by the saved reference's own
identity now.

Accessibility. Every row rendered a button reading "Add", which a screen reader heard as a
list of identical buttons; the buttons now name their agent. The Show more toggle had no
expanded state, so it now carries aria-expanded and aria-controls and can name what it
expands. The logo run exposed nothing: a logo-less app was aria-hidden and the "+N" tooltip
hung off a non-focusable span, so neither name was reachable. It is a labeled list now.

ExpandableDescription measured once. The answer depends on the element's own box, so a
drawer that opens at another width kept the first measurement. It re-measures on resize.

Two more, not defects but wrong all the same. The drawer reset its search only when the
user closed it, so a close driven by the parent kept the last query; destroyOnClose unmounts
the drawer body, not the component that owns the state. And the SubagentList story used
`ref_by: "version"`, which cannot occur: the axis is "variant" or "environment", and the
version is a field on the variant axis. The story looked right while exercising an
impossible wire shape.

* feat(playground): wire the add-subagent drawer to real data

The drawer was a design until now; the Subagents plus still opened the old master/detail
selector. It opens the new one, against the project's real agents.

The data it needed did not exist. A row shows the model an agent runs on and the apps it has
connected, and WorkflowReferenceUI is artifact-scoped: it carries id, slug, name, description
and type, while those two facts belong to a particular revision. Appending them to the
artifact would have shown one revision's model beside a reference bound to another.

The seam is one batched hook, useSubagentCatalog, on the existing bridge. It reads the SAME
cached latest-revision fetch the type badges already perform, so a row's model, its connected
apps, its type and its variant binding all arrive with no extra request. Resolving them per
row would have fired one request per visible agent. Icons and logos are read through derived
atoms over the whole set for the same reason.

Subagents now means agent workflows only, which is what the drawer's copy always claimed. A
saved reference can still point at a prompt, a custom workflow or an evaluator, because that
was allowed before. Those stay listed and removable, tagged "not an agent", so a reference
saved under the old rules cannot become invisible. Only resolved types are tagged, so a slow
revision fetch never labels a good agent.

Two things the wiring had to get right. An agent is no longer offered itself, which would
build a reference loop the runner cannot run. And a batch add runs sequentially, because
handleAddWorkflowReference re-reads the freshest config after resolving an input schema, so
firing several in parallel would let the last write win and drop the rest.

Removal is by slug, not by name: a reference's display name is editable and need not match
the workflow it points at, so removing by name could miss the entry or hit a different tool.

Verified against the running stack, not only in Storybook: the drawer lists 13 real agents
with their real models and app logos, excludes the agent being edited, excludes evaluators,
and a full add-then-remove round trip writes a revision each way and is reflected in the
panel.

WorkflowReferenceSelector and its story are removed. Nothing reaches them any more.

* refactor(playground): act on a four-angle cleanup review of the subagents work

Three of the findings were live defects, not tidying.

The provider mark never drew. LLMIconMap is keyed by display names ("Anthropic"), while a saved
config stores the lowercase family ("anthropic"), so every row fell through to the generic glyph.
getProviderIcon normalizes the key and already exists for exactly this; the sibling prompt control
uses it. The bridge now reads the provider through connectionFromConfig too, rather than by hand.

A closed drawer fetched. The container is mounted for the panel's whole life, and nothing in it
was gated on `open`, so it subscribed to one Composio catalog query per distinct connected app
across every agent in the project, before the drawer had ever been opened. Every subscription is
gated on `open` now, and icons resolve for the listed agents rather than for every workflow in the
project, including the prompts and evaluators the list never draws.

The "not an agent" mark never appeared. ConnectedSubagentList resolved types by passing
bridge.workflows, which stays empty until the picker calls activate(). So useSubagentCatalog now
takes SLUGS: the saved list passes the handful it already has, the picker passes the project's.
That also removes a duplicated slug-key derivation.

The rest is cleanup the same review asked for.

One nameless subagent used to light BOTH section headers with two different messages, because the
integrations branch re-scanned the array the subagents branch had just scanned.

Four places read a reference's slug by hand, without the `type === "reference"` guard that
toolReferenceSlug carries, so a non-reference tool holding a `slug` could be mistaken for one. All
four go through the helper. subagentKey also tested `t.variant`, which no writer emits: the writer
saves `variant_id`.

ExpandableDescription attached a ResizeObserver per row, which the permission drawer pays 50 times
over on open. Only a multi-line clamp can change its answer on resize, and those lists are short,
so the single-line case measures once as it did before the extraction.

Dead after this branch deleted its only caller: the whole useWorkflowTypes path (the hook, the
evaluator-label atom, humanizeEvaluatorKey, the evaluatorKey field, and the bridge contract
member), four handlers on useAgentTools that fed the removed dropdown, a pass-through
IntegrationSection wrapper, and props on ExpandableDescription and LogoMarks that no call site
passes.

CHANGE_FIELD_FOR_SECTION was a one-entry lookup table read twice; it is a function now. The two
subagent-list branches shared seven props by copy; they share one object.

* feat(playground): draw a saved subagent as an agent, not as a workflow reference

A subagent added to the config panel rendered through describeTool, which classifies a raw tool
entry. For a reference that means the internal vocabulary: a "workflow" tag, a solid teal square,
and a monospace name. None of it is true on this surface. The reader is looking at another agent.

describeSubagent replaces it. No type tag at all, because "workflow" is how the entry is stored
and nothing user-meaningful replaces it. The name renders as prose. The chip is the agent's OWN
icon: its chosen colour at a low alpha behind a glyph in that same colour, with the dark-mode
lightening agentIconChrome already handles, falling back to the section's robot glyph for an agent
that never picked one.

Getting that icon needed one more field. A saved reference stores only a slug, and an agent's icon
is keyed by workflow id, so the catalog now carries the workflow id it already had in hand from
the revision it fetches. No extra request. ItemDescriptor grew an optional chip class and style so
the row can paint itself; every other item keeps the solid type square.

The rest is the row geometry from the same handoff, applied to the shared row rather than to
subagents alone, because these are the config panel's rows and one section looking different from
its neighbours is the problem, not the fix: 8px radius, the secondary border, a fill on hover
instead of a border-colour change, 10px vertical padding with a tighter right edge for the action
cluster, a 13px name, the tertiary token on the description, and a 13px caret. The trash becomes a
24px ghost button with a red hover fill, because a hover-only 14px glyph with no box is a small
thing to hit and a destructive action deserves a clear state.

Checked on the running stack: the panel shows the new row, the word "workflow" is gone, and the
Integrations rows read consistently with it.

* fix(playground): stop persisting a reference field the SDK contract forbids

An independent review found this and I verified it against the contract before changing
anything.

A saved workflow reference carried variant_id. ReferenceToolConfig does not have that field, and
ToolConfigBase sets extra="forbid", so an entry holding it fails validation. Nothing consumes it
either: the callback identity is workflow.variant.{slug} or workflow.variant.{slug}.{version}, and
the server parser reads only those. The field predates this branch, but the old selector that
wrote it is gone, so this path owns it now.

References bind by slug on the variant axis with no pinned version, which the server resolves as
the workflow's latest revision. That is the same revision the catalog fetched to build the row, so
what the author saw is what the agent calls. The variant id is gone from the catalog too, since
nothing needs it.

Proof on the running stack, in one saved config: the entry added before this fix still carries
variant_id, and the entry added after it does not.

Two more from the same review.

The provider mark still did not draw. connectionFromConfig reads a ModelRef object, and I was
handing it the model string, so the provider came back null and the row drew the fallback glyph
again. This is the second time the same display broke in a different place.

Overlapping writes could lose one. Every add reads the freshest config and appends, so two rapid
clicks both start from the same array. The sequential loop only protected a single Add all. The
drawer now allows one write at a time and disables every add and remove until it settles.

Naming, also from the review. chipClassName and chipStyle become avatarClassName and avatarStyle,
because "chip" was implementation vocabulary for what the row calls an avatar. useSubagentCatalog
becomes useWorkflowReferenceCatalog, because it deliberately resolves non-agent workflows too.

* fix(playground): drop the forbidden variant field on the reference edit path too

The add path stopped persisting variant_id, but the edit form for an existing reference still
wrote it, so opening a subagent and changing its binding put the field straight back. It is now
deleted on every write from that form, which also cleans an entry saved before the field was known
to be invalid.

The variant selection stays as UI state, because it drives which variant the picker shows as
chosen. It is simply never persisted: ReferenceToolConfig forbids unknown fields, has no
variant_id, and the server resolves workflow.variant.{slug}[.{version}].

* feat(playground): rebuild the subagent detail, and always run the agent's latest revision

A saved subagent opened the old workflow-reference editor: an exposed tool name, the resolved
input schema, a Form/JSON toggle, and a "Reference by / Pinned / Deployed" axis picker. None of
that told the reader when to call this agent.

The panel is now what the handoff asks for. One editable field, the description, because that is
what the model reads to decide when to call the subagent. Under it, a read-only card: the model
with its provider mark, the instruction file clamped to four lines behind a fade with Show full
instructions, the connected apps with their real logos and the permission each was granted, and
the skills as pills. Every row says so plainly when it is empty.

The identity sits in the drawer's own header band, next to the close button, the way the board
draws it: the agent's icon, its name, "Subagent" underneath, and Open agent on the right. It is
NOT repeated in the body.

A subagent always runs the LATEST revision of the agent it points at. That is now a property of
the product, not a choice: the version, revision and environment controls are gone. A helper agent
that silently goes stale is worse than one that improves with its owner.

Three drawer rules became per item rather than per kind, because one kind now holds both a
two-pane editor and a plain panel. A tool's parameter editor keeps its 800px width and its
full-bleed body; a subagent gets ordinary drawer padding and the default width. Without that split
the panel rendered edge to edge with no margin at all.

The detail is a cached hook keyed by slug, so the header and the body read one result rather than
fetching twice. The integration logos are resolved in the view, because the bridge knows WHICH
apps an agent connects but a logo and a display name come from the catalog, which only a component
can read.

Checked on the desktop and on /m. Mobile supplies no route for an agent page, so Open agent hides
there rather than guessing one. Its Integrations section shows rows with no add button, because
mobile has no gateway bridge, which is the gating this branch added earlier working as intended.

* refactor(playground): cut the added comments to one line each

The frontend guide allows at most one short line per comment. The subagents work
had grown multi-line blocks that narrated why in prose. Trim them, keep a second
line only where a real trap needs it, and drop three stale story notes that said
the barrel does not export what it now exports.

* fix(playground): enforce always-latest on every subagent write

A Codex review found the description edit path spread the whole saved entry
back, so a legacy `variant_id`, `version` or `environment` survived an edit

in the UI able to see or clear it. Both writes now go through one

test(gate): pin the first-call placeholder race with a standing cell

A free-credits user on cloud hit a 401 because a fresh Daytona sandbox's first
model call raced the asynchronous substitution of its Daytona Secret: the
provider received the raw dtn_secret_<id> placeholder. The product then told the
user to add their own OpenAI key, which was wrong three ways.

The race itself is a vendor-side timing property and will happen again. What
this cell pins is that it is never reported as the user's fault: a placeholder
401 must carry the runner's credential_delivery_failed code and its retry copy.

The cell mints a new workflow so the sandbox is necessarily cold, sends one
short message so the first model call lands as early as possible, and asserts
the stored turn row came back. It fails when a run advises adding a key while
the underlying refusal carries the placeholder signature. On a local deployment
it also counts Received=dtn_ lines in the litellm-proxy container and reports
the count as diagnostic, never as a verdict.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0165tsjmvf3qvTPFcb9EV44g

test(gate): sweep the runner log for reconciliation DISAGREE lines

The runner holds two views of a session's identity: the coordinator's
configFingerprint decision, and the reconciliation router's per-facet digests.
When the two drift apart, a request that should reuse a warm sandbox instead
cold-evicts it. That is the over-eviction family fixed in v0.114.4.

The drift is invisible from the wire. The turn still succeeds; it just paid for
a rebuild it did not need. A DISAGREE line never fails a turn by design, because
the shadow must never break a run, which is exactly why it needs a sweep.

Keyed on the marker logReconcileShadow writes in reconciliation-router.ts:

  [reconcile] shadow key=... decision=...(...) plan=...(...) DISAGREE facets=[...]

The padded DISAGREE token cannot match the word DISAGREEMENTS in the router's
own comments, and agree / n/a(continuity) lines are correctly ignored. Exits
0 PASS, 1 FAIL with the offending lines, 2 SKIP when the log is not reachable.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0165tsjmvf3qvTPFcb9EV44g

test(gate): a malformed harness must fail closed, never default

The dangerous failure for a malformed harness value is not a crash. It is a
default: a config the platform cannot read, quietly resolved to whichever
harness the code falls back to, running a full turn and storing output the user
never asked for. Afterwards the stored row carries a real harness_kind, so
nothing downstream can tell it apart from a run the user configured.

The cell drives three unreadable harness blocks (a wrong-type value, an unknown
string, a null kind) at both the commit API and the live invoke, and records
which boundary refused rather than demanding a particular one. A refusal further
out is better, not worse. It fails if a turn executes and stores output.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0165tsjmvf3qvTPFcb9EV44g

test(gate): a Daytona Secret must not outlive the run that created it

A Daytona run stores the real model key as a Daytona Secret and gives the
sandbox only a placeholder. Teardown deletes the Secret. When teardown misses
one, the key stays live in the Daytona organization with no sandbox left to use
it: a leak no product surface shows, that grows with every run.

Standalone rather than folded into matrix_w1_daytona.py. The assertion needs a
second credential the rest of the gate does not use (a Daytona API key), so
folding it in would give an existing green cell a new way to SKIP for a reason
unrelated to what it tests. It also needs an eviction step W1 does not want, and
a before/after inventory around the whole journey.

There is no product route that closes a session, so the cell uses the product's
own teardown trigger: a second turn with a changed configuration, which the
runner reads as a config mismatch and answers by evicting the sandbox.

fix(runner): classify a direct-provider credential race honestly, once per session

On a Daytona run the model key never enters the sandbox. It is a Daytona
Secret, and the sandbox holds a dtn_secret_<id> placeholder that Daytona
substitutes into egress asynchronously. When the first model call beats that
propagation the provider refuses the raw placeholder with a 401.

Two layers were supposed to catch that, and on a direct provider BOTH missed.

The detector only recognized the race when the error body echoed the
placeholder. The litellm credits proxy echoes it; no direct provider does.
api.anthropic.com answers a bad bearer with "Invalid bearer token" and no echo
at all, and OpenAI's echo is masked ("dtn_secr***...cdef"), which no longer
contains the literal dtn_secret_ the signature looked for. So every direct-path
placeholder 401 fell through to the generic auth branch and told the user to add
a key they already had.

The preflight is wired on the direct path, but its probe is OpenAI-shaped:
POST {baseUrl}/chat/completions against api.anthropic.com returns 404 with an
empty body, so it fails open on probe 1 and logs nothing. Fixing the URL would
not help, because Anthropic echoes nothing for the masked-echo instrument to
convict on.

This gives the classifier a second, body-independent signal: whether this run's
model credential rode a Daytona Secret delivered inside the propagation window.
It also widens the placeholder signature to catch OpenAI's masked echo, so the
direct OpenAI path is self-diagnosing from the body again rather than depending
on timing. Both stay anchored on Daytona's dtn_ prefix, which cannot occur in a
provider key.

THE INVERSE CASE, and why the counter exists. A genuinely wrong key produces a
byte-identical refusal on the direct path. Telling it to retry is a dead end:
a failed turn is not parkable, so the sandbox is DELETED, the retry
cold-acquires, the freshness window re-arms, and the same advice repeats
forever. One report per session bounds it. The second identical failure, on a
second fresh sandbox, is far better explained by the key, so it falls through to
the ordinary add-a-key advice. A bad key costs exactly one wasted retry; a real
race still recovers silently, because the retry lands on a fresh sandbox.

The counter lives on SessionContinuityStore because that is the only state with
the right lifetime: it outlives the environment (which the failed turn deletes),
dies with the conversation, and losing it is harmless.

fix(frontend): drop the quadratic backtrack from the file-activity match

`namedFileActivity` matched `/^(.*?)\s+(?:an?|the)\s+file$/` against a tool's
humanized activity. The lazy prefix and the `\s+` after it both match a space,
so the prefix can end anywhere inside a whitespace run and the engine retries
every split — quadratic on an activity that is mostly spaces (CodeQL
js/polynomial-redos, flagged high on the v0.114.5 release PR).

Read the parse from the end off a word split instead: the last word must be
"file", the one before it an article, and what remains is the prefix. Same
result on every activity the tool registry produces, linear on anything else.

fix(runner): let the credential preflight judge providers that do not echo the key

The Daytona credential preflight convicted a stuck sandbox only when the
provider echoed a MASKED placeholder back. That instrument is blind on every
provider that answers a bad bearer without naming it. Production runner logs
for 2026-09-01..02 show 10 user-visible failures on the direct OpenRouter
connection: the probe found nothing to judge, failed open on probe 1, the run
proceeded, and the first model call returned a 401 that the classifier could
only report as a credential delivery failure. Anthropic and Gemini have the
same blind spot.

Add a second, body-independent instrument. The runner holds the real key when
it creates the Daytona Secret, so the preflight makes one control call of its
own to the same URL with the same body, concurrently with the sandbox probe.
The sandbox probe now also captures the HTTP status. A sandbox 401 with no echo
beside a control call that was ACCEPTED means the sandbox sent something the
provider refused while the real key works, and the only other thing the sandbox
can send is the raw placeholder. That counts toward conviction under the same
consecutive-probe rule and the same 10s budget as the masked echo. A control
call that is refused (401 or 403) means the key itself is bad, so the preflight
fails open and the turn classifier gives the add-a-key advice. A control call
that errors, times out, or returns no status also fails open.

Add the Anthropic request shape (/v1/messages, x-api-key, anthropic-version)
for both the sandbox probe and the control call. Every other provider stays on
the OpenAI-compatible shape, which covers the LiteLLM credits proxy, OpenAI and
OpenRouter. Gemini is not covered here: its auth rides a query parameter, so it
needs its own shape.

The key value has one destination, the control call's request header. The
sandbox command carries only the env var name, and every log line goes through
a redactor.

fix(runner): rebuild a stuck sandbox on the same Daytona Secret, and allow a third attempt

On Daytona the model key never enters the sandbox. The runner creates a Daytona
Secret and the sandbox holds a placeholder that Daytona substitutes on egress.
Some sandboxes never receive that wiring. The credential preflight convicts such
a sandbox in about ten seconds and the acquire path rebuilds.

Production runner logs from 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-02 show the rebuild was stuck
again in 4 of 7 cases. Every rebuild followed the same sequence: destroy the
stuck sandbox, DELETE its Secret, allocate a NEW Secret for the same host within
one second, then create the next sandbox against that new Secret. Daytona support
confirmed on 2026-08-31 that a new sandbox on the SAME Secret works. The runner
never tried that case.

The convicted sandbox is now destroyed while its Secret allocation is KEPT, and
that allocation is handed to the next acquire attempt. The retry's provider
mounts it as-is and makes no Secret create call. Ownership passes to the retry's
registry entry, which deletes the Secret at its own teardown exactly as before.
When no attempt adopts the allocation, because the attempts are exhausted, the
signal aborted, or an attempt failed before create, the acquire path releases it.
The release is idempotent and skips an allocation a live sandbox already holds.

The Secret is still deleted only after Daytona confirms the sandbox is absent.
The delete order in cleanupAfterSandbox is unchanged.

STUCK_ACQUIRE_ATTEMPTS goes from 2 to 3 as a safety net behind the fix. The
rebuild log line names the counts only. No id, name, placeholder, or value is
logged.

Tests: a new unit file pins the facade behavior (retain on destroy, create from
an inherited allocation with zero Secret API calls, a release that respects
adoption) and the acquire behavior (one allocation across a stuck attempt and a
healthy retry, one delete at teardown, and three attempts when every sandbox is
stuck). All 2635 runner unit tests and tsc pass.

fix(runner): narrow the preflight differential to documented auth endpoints

Act on the Codex review of the credential preflight.

The differential no longer reads "any status but 401 or 403" as proof that a
key works. Each covered provider now has a documented non-generation auth
endpoint, and the preflight reads its status alone: OpenRouter GET /key,
Anthropic GET /v1/models?limit=1, OpenAI GET /models. 200 is accepted, 401 is
refused, and everything else, 403 and 3xx and 404 and 405 and 429 and 5xx and a
timeout, is unknown and fails open with a log line that names the status. The
sandbox probe uses the same endpoint, so both sides of the comparison ask the
same question.

The differential applies only to those three providers on a direct deployment.
A custom gateway, the LiteLLM credits proxy included, keeps the POST of an
empty body to /chat/completions and masked-echo-only conviction, and makes no
runner call at all. So does any direct provider outside the three.

The module doc now says plainly what the differential measures: a difference
between two request contexts, attributed to the credential. An IP allowlist, a
WAF rule, or a regional block would convict a healthy sandbox. Three things
bound that. Only a positive auth answer counts, a wrong verdict costs a rebuild
rather than a failed run, and the rule reaches only the three pinned providers.

Also from the review:

- The runner's own request sets redirect: "error", so a 3xx can never send the
  real key to another host. It cancels the response body once the status is
  read.
- One deadline. Every sandbox probe's curl timeout and the runner call are
  capped by what is left of the grace, with a one second floor.
- One AbortController for the runner call, aborted in a finally so every exit
  path releases it, and composed with the acquire signal so a cancelled run
  does not leave a request in flight.
- The log redactor covers any non-empty key value, with no length rule.
- The credential's binding name is checked against a shell-safe variable name
  before it enters the command string. A name that fails fails the preflight
  open and runs nothing.

fix(runner): stop a stale cleanup timer from destroying a reconnected sandbox

Codex's third pass found a race in the cleanup retry added by the previous
commit. The retry callback clears its own timer handle before it awaits the
destroy, so a reconnect arriving in that window finds nothing to cancel, bumps

waiting. The reconnect succeeds and never cancels the replacement, which later

nothing else can arm behind it. Both steps are the same two lines, so they are
one named helper with the reason written down.

cleanup itself, so a replacement armed while it waited is either superseded by
its success, which removes the registry entry, or is the very retry its own
failure would have armed.

option Codex offered, does not fix this on its own. The reconnect would cancel a
handle for a timer that has already fired, the cleanup would still arm the
replacement afterwards, and the reconnect would still not know about it.

`[DEPRECATED] atomFamily is deprecated and will be removed in v3` at module
