agents" is not offered until there is one.

So FirstRunScreen, FirstRunComposer, their copy and their states are
deleted, and `homeSurface` moves to the home feature it now serves: it
only decides whether we know enough to draw Home yet. Its two real rules
survive — an error is never read as emptiness, and an empty list that is
still resolving holds rather than flashing the wrong tab.

The tab and the composer's mode are read once at mount, which is when the
answer is known: Home does not render until the list has resolved.

feat(frontend): give the agent kebab open and archive

Copy ID goes: an id is a debugging detail, and the slug beside it is the
one people quote. Open configuration arrives, dropped on a surface that
passes no handler — the overview itself.

Delete becomes Archive agent, with the archive mark. The verb behind it
has always been `archiveWorkflow` and the modal it opens is already
titled Archive, so the menu was the only thing calling it a delete;
AgentCard's own menu now uses the same words and marks.

The content also forwards onCloseAutoFocus, which is what lets a host
start an inline rename from the menu: the editor must not mount inside
the menu's focus trap.

feat(frontend): give the sessions table a Status column where there is room

The dot carried the whole status, so reading it meant hovering for the tooltip or grouping by Status. From sm up the table now has a Status column: the dot and the word beside it, which is the shape the automations table next door already uses. A dot and a coloured word, never a pill, because the column is read down and a stack of pills reads as a stack of buttons.

A phone keeps the dot beside the title and no column. A fourth reading column at 375px would cost the title the width it needs to be a title, and the word is still in the tooltip and the grouping.

SessionRowStatusMeta gains textClassName alongside dotClassName. The two are not the same colour and should not be: the dot is a mark, so it takes the vivid run-status hue, and #F79009 as 13px type on white is a smear. The word takes the readable semantic text token. Waiting and Running carry colour; the rest are states rather than calls to action, so they read as muted as the timestamp beside them.

fix(frontend): focus the composer from an agent row, and follow the roster

Binding an agent is half the sentence, so the caret goes where the other
half is typed. Templates and "+ New agent" already did this; agent rows
did not, which made them the one row in the list that left you nowhere.

Reading the roster once at mount was also wrong. The list can arrive
empty and fill a moment later, and the snapshot then left the page stuck
on templates with a full roster sitting behind the other tab — which is
exactly what it did on a cold load. The tab and the binding DERIVE from
the roster now, with an explicit choice outliving it: null means follow
the data.

feat(frontend): match the New agent menu to the design copy

Blank agent becomes New agent over one line of what it does, and the
entry takes a tile like the templates under it so the menu reads as one
list of alternatives rather than a button above a list.

fix(frontend): match the session row kebab to the automations one

Three ways they had drifted, all in the sessions copy.

The glyph size was a `size={16}` prop, and the button's own `[&_svg:not([class*='size-'])]:size-3` beat the attribute it produces. The prop did nothing and the icon rendered at 12px, two pixels smaller than the automations kebab rather than the two bigger it was meant to be. It is `className="size-3.5"` now, the way the automations button already writes it: three dots read smaller than a glyph that fills its box, so matching by measurement mismatches by eye.

The hover fill was the button default rather than the `foreground/10` the automations kebab uses, and the glyph was missing `aria-hidden` beside a button that already carries a label.

fix(frontend): act on CodeRabbit's review of Home

Two of these were mine to begin with.

Hiding "Your agents" for an empty roster also hid the tab the loading,
empty and error slots render in, so a FAILED fetch showed the templates
list with no message and no retry — the one case `resolveHomeSurface`
keeps on Home precisely so it can be retried. The tab now exists whenever
the host has something to say there.

And the review pass that deleted `onStartError` as dead API took the
try/catch with it. `RichChatInput` neither awaits nor catches `onSubmit`,
so a rejecting host became an unhandled rejection.

The rest CodeRabbit found on its own:

- A template's instruction was dropped when it was picked before the lazy
  `RichChatInput` chunk resolved: one frame was enough on a warm load and
  not on a cold one, and create mode then submitted empty text with only
  the template's name. The seed retries until the handle exists, bounded.
- A cancelled navigation RESOLVES false rather than throwing, so catching
  alone cleared the attachments while the task sat unplayed in the stash.
  The same hazard `useNewAgentAction` already documents.
- 64 bars at 2.5px with a 1px gap need 223px, and the floors pushed the
  last bar off the right edge below that. Both minimums go.
- An analyser that cannot be built leaves the microphone open for the
  length of the dictation with nothing measuring it.
- `outline-none` with no replacement left the rows, tabs, New agent and
  the retry button with no visible focus for a keyboard.

fix(frontend): stop the first row touching a sticky list header

A sticky header drops its own bottom margin, or a 4px slot of rows shows
through as they pass under it. The first run pays it back as padding
instead, so a row's hover fill no longer sits flush on the rule.

feat(frontend): lead a session row with what kind of session it is

Moving the status into its own column left the name flush against the column edge, and with it went the one mark that separated a chat you started from a run an automation started. Two lists in one column read as one long list.

From sm up the cell leads with the kind: a chat bubble or a bolt, the same two marks the Type facet offers, so the filter and the row agree. A phone keeps the status dot there instead, since it has no Status column to carry it and status is the thing worth knowing at that width.

feat(frontend): pick the agent in the dock, and lead the picker with New agent

Two pieces of design feedback on Home, both the same principle: an
affordance needs a signifier.

The dock named the bound agent as plain text. Nothing said it could
change, and the change lived in a list a screen's height away — people
clicked the name, found nothing, and assumed a bug. It is the app's one
AgentPicker again, as a pill, beside the thing it changes. The rows below
still bind; this is the second way in.

The ✕ on that name quietly opened create mode, a second hidden
affordance where a close control was expected to close. It is gone.
Creating is the picker's FIRST row instead, behind a `createFirst` prop
on AgentPicker that defaults off: a picker that mostly chooses keeps
creating in its footer, and only a surface whose composer can just as
well describe a new agent wants it leading.

The picker's search glass also comes in from a 28px box to 20px. It
matched the row chips' width, but a 14px glyph centred in 28px read as
a gap between the icon and the field, and a search field is not a row.

fix(frontend): read a list table from its own edge

The header, the group headings and the rows each inset their content by
8px, so everything inside the table started 8px in from the column the
page title and the toolbar keep — the first heading and the first cell
under it both sat off that line.

The inset goes from all of them at once. That is the part that matters:
the header's content box has to stay identical to a row's, or the two
resolve their grid tracks differently and every column but the first
drifts off its cells.

A row then takes the space back as bleed rather than as inset: its box
grows 12px on each side and its padding gives the same 12px back, so the
hover fill clears the text it covers while the text itself stays on the
table's edge, and the content box — and so the tracks — never move.

fix(frontend): clear the search draft when a route scope applies

A keystroke already on the debounce survived a scope reset. applySessionScopeAtom clears the search atom, but if the atom was already empty its value never changed, so nothing told the field — and 300ms later the pending write landed and re-narrowed the list the route had just scoped.

The hook cannot see this: an unchanged value is not an event. The screen knows a scope was applied, so it clears the draft alongside it, which cancels the pending write.

revert(frontend): keep the picker's New agent row in its footer

The leading-row variant added a prop for one host to opt into. The
footer row already existed, sits under a rule for the reason the picker
documents, and is what every other picker shows — one shape for the
control everywhere beats a second position for one surface. `createFirst`
goes; Home uses the footer.

feat(frontend): model how the mobile agents roster is cut and narrowed

The view a reader sets — which roster, whose agents, what state, how the
rows group — and the pure derivation over it, kept out of the screen so
the screen renders what this returns rather than deriving it mid-render.
The same split sessionListView.ts makes next door.

Type is deliberately absent from the predicates: it picks WHICH roster
the screen fetches, so rows already match it by the time they arrive.

Status is the one state an agent actually has here — whether a session of
its own is blocked on a person. The design's Active/Paused/Needs-attention
belongs to an automation, which has a trigger to pause; an agent has none.

feat(frontend): reorganize the navigation rail to the Sidebar Reorg design

Brings the rail to option 1b of the Claude Design "Sidebar Reorg" project, and
moves three things that were sitting in the wrong place.

Density. Rows are 26px at 13px where they were 28px at 14px, the brand row is
32px with an 80x18 wordmark instead of 48px, and session titles drop to 12px
with 10px status glyphs, so the session pane reads as a list under the nav
rather than as more nav.

Session rows line up with the nav. The 22px indent and the vertical guide line
are gone for groups that carry no collapse control, which is what pushed every
status dot out of the column the Home, Agents and Sessions icons share. Keyed
on alwaysOpen rather than on the Sessions key: a group you cannot collapse is a
section of the rail, and its rows are rail rows. The Evaluation group, which you
do open, keeps its indent and its line.

Agents is a plain row. Its dynamic child list is gone; an agent list in the rail
was a second, shorter answer to a question the Agents page already answers in
full, and the caret it needed made the row look like the Sessions group, which
is the rail's only real list. That removed the last caller of
sidebarAgentRanksAtomFamily, so it goes too, along with withManualAgentRanks and
the 'agents' drag zone behind it. The agent headings under Sessions keep their
own zone and their own counts.

Releases leave the banner queue. They read as a "What's new?" list inside the
help menu now. A release is news, not a task: it does not need clearing, and
eleven of them queued two at a time made it feel like one. The queue keeps
star-repo and the trial/upgrade banners EE injects, which are tasks.

Help becomes an icon button on the switcher row, drawing the same flyout the
collapsed rail draws. Book a call comes out and Keyboard shortcuts takes its
place, which gives the shortcuts sheet a visible way in; it had been reachable
only through a bare '?' hotkey that teaches nobody.

Session search. A magnifier beside the filter opens a palette backed by a
debounced server search. Filtering the rail's own fifty-row window would search
the top of the list and call everything else missing, which is the one case a
search exists for.

The rail's filter uses the shared menu. SessionFilterMenu went from 220 lines to
a section map over @agenta/ui/filter-menu, the same panel the automations list
opens, and the superseded presentational/filter/FilterMenu is deleted; this was
its last caller.

Dark selection stops shouting. The selected row painted an olive wash with
accent-yellow text and no ring, the loudest thing on a rail whose job is to sit
still, and it disagreed with light. One rule in both themes now: a raised
surface, a hairline, and the text left alone. Dark is #242424 on the #101010
rail with a #292929 ring, changed at the source in palette.ts with the tokens
regenerated.

Verified on the running mobile app throughout, measuring geometry in the DOM:
session glyphs and nav icons both at left 20px, brand row exactly 32px,
collapsed icons 28px with 4px between them, and the three bottom controls
stepping evenly. tsc clean on oss and mobile, eslint clean, 82 navigation unit
tests pass (down from 86: the four withManualAgentRanks cases described a helper
that no longer exists).

test(frontend): expect the pinned query to override the surface's narrowing

pinnedSessionListArgs now clears the activity window and the archive-only view and turns
includeArchived on, for the reason the implementation states: a pin is an explicit request,
and each of those would drop a row the reader asked to keep. The test still expected the
surface's own values to pass through untouched.

fix(frontend): keep the dock a picker while creating

Create mode turned the dock back into a label, so the only visible way
out of "New agent" was the list below. It is the same picker with
nothing bound: choosing an agent leaves the mode.

Also drops a `createFirst` guard that survived resolving this lane over
the automations lane's edit to the same footer.

feat(frontend): read the creators and the archived agents a roster needs

Creators come from the org's member roster under the same cache key the
settings screen already reads, so arriving from Settings costs no request
and the two surfaces cannot disagree about a name.

Archived agents need a second query: the shared apps list omits
include_archived because the nav rail reads absence there as archived
(#6457), so flipping it would break the rail. It is gated on the facet
and keyed under agent-workflows, so archiving an agent invalidates both
this list and the live one in the same pass.

feat(frontend): remove the sidebar banner slot

The rail no longer draws a banner card. The Sidebar Reorg design has no
card there, and after the changelog cards moved into the help menu's
"What's new?" list and the star-repo ask went with them (the same menu
links GitHub), nothing OSS or mobile showed was left.

Drops the banner model (`@agenta/navigation` banners: config types,
priority/dismissal atoms, the `additionalBannersAtom` seam), the
`SidebarBanner`/`SidebarBanners` renderers, the OSS
`SidePanel/Subscription` shim, and the footer mounts in the desktop
main scope and the mobile scope. The `footer` slot on `SidebarScope`
stays: it is shell contract, not banner code.

EE: its `SidePanel/Subscription` shadow module injected trial/upgrade
banners through the seam removed here, so it goes with this.

revert(frontend): drop the kind glyph from the session row

The bubble before every name said the same thing on every row of a Chat-typed list, and the Type facet already says it once for the whole list. The row leads with the title from sm up; a phone keeps its status dot, which has no column to live in there.

feat(frontend): show the send is in flight on Home

Pressing send on a template or a new agent went quiet for the two or
three seconds it takes to mint the agent and open its session — nothing
spun, nothing disabled, and a second press was possible. The composer's
send button takes a `sending` prop now: the arrow becomes a spinner on
the same filled button, and it refuses another press. Threaded the route
`dictating` already takes, host to button.

The host had the fact all along — `useNewAgentAction.creating` — and
nothing read it. The task path gets its own `starting` flag for the
navigation it makes, which only ever has to come down on failure since
success unmounts the page.

A failed create also said nothing: the spinner stopped and that was all.
It now lands in the same dismissable notice the chat composer docks
above the input for a send that did not go, with the draft kept.

feat(frontend): expose the facts the mobile overview cards read

Additive package changes only: agentConfigSummary names the integration behind each gateway-connection tool, NextTriggersSection's row derivation moves into a useUpcomingTriggers hook a host with its own card chrome can call, and composioLogo is exported for any integration key outside PROVIDERS.

feat(frontend): redesign the mobile agents page

The roster is the shared ListTable — the frame the sessions and
automations lists already use — with this app's columns, the shared agent
kebab, and rename in place from a row rather than through a modal.

Search sits in a ListTableToolbar beside the shared FilterMenu carrying
Created by, Type, Status and Group by. A workflow becomes a row in one
place, so no cell re-derives a creator's name or a waiting count from
lookup maps handed down beside it.

Every state is designed: skeleton, empty, no-match and a failed fetch
with a retry — a request that never answered must not read as an empty
project.

fix(frontend): put the rail's row rhythm back to 28px

Reverts the density pass. Rows return to h-7 / 14px / leading-7 with
their 4px margin, group headings to pt-2, session titles to the row's
own size, and the status glyphs to 12/12/10. The 26px/13px column read
as one packed list with no breathing room next to ChatGPT, Manus and the
rail we shipped before. The alignment work stays: session glyphs still
sit in the nav icons' column, and the logo and collapsed rail keep their
smaller geometry.

feat(frontend): make archived a switch on the sessions filter menu

Archived leaves the Type row — it is a lens over Chat or Automation, not a third type — and becomes an "Only archived" toggle row.

fix(frontend): spin the send button with the ring the chat surfaces use

The four-dot antd spinner was the wrong loader for a 16px glyph swap;
the chat surfaces already load with a CircleNotch ring, so this does too.

It also keeps the filled accent while sending. Lexical empties the
editor on submit, which flipped the button to its inert grey — a spinner
on that said "nothing to do" and "working" at once.

feat(frontend): redesign the mobile agent overview

The overview reads the way the Agent Overview design does: a description and an Open chat verb in the header, Home's composer with voice, then one activity list under Sessions | Automation runs tabs with the shared filter menu (status, window, grouping) instead of two stacked cards. The rail is three soft cards owned by this app — Configuration with stacked integration marks, Files with Open drive, Automations with a clock or bolt per trigger — built on the sessions table's frame and the entity-ui hooks, so no desktop chrome changes. Usage is dropped, as designed.

fix(frontend): read archived agents through the shared classification map

main replaced filterAgentWorkflows(workflows, latestRevisions) with selectAgentWorkflows over
a per-project agent-flags map (#classify agents once per project), and this hook still called
the old name — the mobile typecheck and image build failed on it after the rebase.

ensureAgentFlags is the better fit anyway: the shared map already covers archived workflows,
so the second round trip this hook used to make for their latest revisions is now a cache
hit.

feat(frontend): call tools "integrations" in the mobile app

The gateway-tool surface is a list of connected apps (Gmail, Slack), and "tool"
also names the tool CALLS a transcript shows — two things under one word. This
app now says Integrations for the connected-app concept: the settings tab, its
nav entries, the connections table, and the agent overview's config row.

oss/ee keep their wording, so the rename is a mobile copy layer
(web/mobile/src/lib/integrationsCopy.ts) over shared components that now take an
optional copy prop and default to the old strings.

fix(frontend): give the Agent filter flyout room for a name

The shared filter menu's flyout is 188px, sized for words like "Last
30 days". Agent names are longer — "Search Console Assistant" truncated
to "Search Consol…" — so a section can now ask for a `wide` flyout,
which matches the panel's own 248px. Only the Agent facet opts in, in
the rail's session filter and the sessions page's.

feat(frontend): put the session's status back on its icon

The kind glyph returns, and carries the status on its shoulder the way the original row drew it. The status column keeps the word; the shoulder dot is the at-a-glance mark, and it is what a phone gets in place of the column.

Tightened over the original: the glyph is 15px to match the automations rows, the dot is solid in every state (a hollow ring would be a ring inside a ring at 9px), it takes the same run-status hue the Status column paints, pulses while live, and wears a 2px page-colour ring so it sits on the glyph rather than in it.

fix(frontend): slim the automations list to name and last run on a phone

Below 640px the list keeps name, last run and actions, so it fits the screen without sideways scroll; status, cadence and agent wait on the detail screen.

feat(frontend): edit an agent's description in place on mobile

The description under the overview's title edits the way the name does: tap it (or Edit description in the kebab) and it becomes a one-line input; Enter commits, Esc cancels, blank clears. An agent with no description shows the same line as an 'Add a description' prompt, so the header keeps one shape. The line truncates at the composer column's width.

Package pieces, all additive: useUpdateAgentDescription beside useRenameAgent, an optional Edit description entry on AgentActionsMenu, allowEmpty on useInlineRename, and updateWorkflow treating an empty description as a change rather than skipping the request.

feat(frontend): tighten the session rows

Rows drop from 50px to 40px. ListTable gains a density prop rather than a global change, because the lists it frames are not the same length: sessions runs to hundreds of rows, where 13px above and below each is a screen of air per hundred, while an automations list is a dozen a reader scans once. Compact is 8px; the default is untouched, so the automations and agents tables keep their rhythm.

The skeleton takes the same value as the rows, so loading holds the rhythm the rows arrive in. The rename input drops to the kebab's height, the tallest thing in a resting row, so a row being renamed stays the height of its neighbours.

Its own lane above the agents page: that branch and the sessions one both edit ListTable, in that order, so this had nowhere lower to land without breaking one of them.

feat(frontend): make archived a switch on the agents filter menu

The Type row held only Active/Archived, two entries to say one bit; it is now an "Only archived" toggle row.

chore(frontend): cut the new copy comments to one line

Repo rule (web/AGENTS.md): at most one short line per comment.
fix(frontend): give the automations Agent flyout room for a name

fix(frontend): drop the ring from the session icon's status dot

The page-colour ring read as a dark border around the dot rather than as a gap between it and the glyph. Bare dot, 7px, sat a little closer to the corner.

style(frontend): tighten the Home composer dock

Trim the dock's vertical padding so the agent row reads as a footer, not a second box.

fix(frontend): measure the session tab strip from layout offsets, not scrollWidth

Resizing the configuration pane in /m could crash the page with React error
#185 ("Maximum update depth exceeded"). The tab strip decided whether the New
session (+) overflows from `scrollWidth`, but whether to un-pin it from layout
offsets. The chips are motion layout items: while the strip resizes, their
layout animation holds them on a translate that `scrollWidth` counts as
overflow and offsets do not. The two rules could each be satisfied in turn, so
the (+) moved out of the scroller, the chips re-projected, the next measure
moved it back, and the flips chained synchronously until React gave up. The
throw surfaced inside the (+)'s tooltip trigger ref, which is why the stack
pointed at Radix compose-refs.

Both decisions, and the edge fade, now read the same transform-free content
width. The hysteresis that was always intended holds: the pinned (+) sits
outside the scroller, so `clientWidth` is already net of it.

The regression test mounts a strip that fits, then delivers a resize while
`scrollWidth` is inflated the way an in-flight translate inflates it; on the
old code it reproduces the exact error.

fix(services): route under the public /services prefix without a stripping proxy (#6702)

* fix(services): route under the public /services prefix without a stripping proxy

Traefik and the AWS ALB strip /services before a request reaches the
services container, so its routes live at root. A managed ingress such as
GKE cannot rewrite paths and forwards /services/... verbatim, which answered
404 on every route, including the agent invoke endpoint the playground uses.

Add an ASGI middleware that strips the prefix inbound, in a loop and without
redirects, the same way the api's ApiPrefixStripMiddleware does. The prefix
comes from AGENTA_SERVICES_PATH_PREFIX, default /services; an empty value
turns the strip off. Registered last so it runs before auth and routing.

fix(frontend): lay settings tables out for the viewport they are on

On a phone, Settings > AI providers rendered its six desktop columns at their
desktop widths — 1026px of table behind a 374px scroller — so only Provider and
part of Name showed, and with no visible scrollbar the table read as cut off
rather than scrollable.

The shared data table now adapts. A column can name the narrowest viewport it
belongs to (`responsive: "md"`, Tailwind's breakpoints); below it the column
is dropped and the column-settings menu no longer offers it, so a phone shows
what identifies and acts on a row. Flexible columns give way together, down to
sixty percent of their declared width, before the table overflows — a
two-column table fits by trimming a name, a six-column one still scrolls
rather than squeezing every column past reading. What still overflows gets an
edge fade on the scroller, the cue the invisible scrollbar never gave; the
border moves outside the scroller so the fade dissolves columns, not the
frame.

The providers page marks Credential, Active models and Created as `md`
columns. Every other settings table gets the fade and the bounded shrink for
free and is otherwise unchanged at desktop widths.

fix(frontend): refuse an image in a reply whose target names a host An agent reply could carry `![diagram](..//evil.com/x.png)`. rehype-harden parses that and emits the pathname `//evil.com/x.png`, a protocol-relative URL, so the browser fetched the image from the other host and Streamdown's image renderer offered a download button whose fallback is `window.open` on the raw target. A click on "download this image" landed on a site the markdown never showed. #6675 closed the same escape for links at the anchor; the image renderer is Streamdown's own and was left alone (#6680). The refusal now happens in the rehype tree, before harden and before any renderer sees the node. `rehypeRefuseHostImages` turns an `img` whose `src` the anchor gate's predicate recognises into the span harden leaves for a link it refuses — "alt [blocked]" with the target in its title — and sits next to the anchor respelling in the shared pipeline, so both hosts get it. An explicit https:// image stays allowed, as a scheme URL does for links. Reproduced on /m: the reply rendered . After: "diagram [blocked]", no image, no button. Fixes #6680

fix(frontend): report a session rename whose header write did not land

A rename of a session open in the desktop's local cache reported success
whether or not the header write landed. renameSessionAtomFamily set the
title optimistically and swallowed the write's answer, commitRename dropped
the cache write's result, and SessionTabLabel never looked at it. The tab
kept the new name until the next list read quietly put the old one back.

The atom now resolves the write's outcome and restores the previous title
when the header refuses it; commitRename treats a false from the cache
write as the failure it is; SessionTabLabel awaits the rename and shows
"Couldn't rename this session" when it did not land, the same message
the shared inline rename shows on the other surfaces.

fix(frontend): name the agent of a variant- or revision-bound automation

Triggers written through the SDK or API bind only a variant or a revision; the backend stores
the references as sent. The automations list looked that leaf id up in the agent roster, which
is keyed by workflow id, and read every such row as "Unknown agent" (#6820).

useAutomations now resolves the leaf id to its workflow through the workflow entity's existing
per-id queries before any row is read, so the label, search, agent filter, grouping and the
detail screen all key the same roster. The editor waits for that resolution before seeding its
draft, so a Save can never rebind to the leaf id.

fix(mobile): clear the composer attachments when the message leaves

Sending with an attachment from Home or the agent overview left the file in the chat composer (#6777). Those hand-offs cleared the tray only after router.push resolved, but the chat route seeds its own tray from the per-session store on mount — before that promise settles — so the clear landed on the unmounting hook and never reached the store. Clear before navigating and put the rows back with restoreAttachments when the hand-off fails.

The chat composer had the milder version of the same ordering: it cleared after the send promise, which waits for run admission, while the text and echo left instantly. Clear before the await there too, restoring on a refused send.

fix(frontend): make the connect dock's Retry reuse the pending connection

Retry re-created the connection under the same fixed slug, which the API
rejects with 409, so every retry after a closed, blocked or timed-out OAuth
popup failed. The flow now looks up the row the first attempt left and
refreshes it (fresh redirect_url, same row), and settles as connected when
the row was already authorized elsewhere.

The popup is now opened synchronously inside the tap and pointed at the
redirect once the request resolves: WebKit blocks window.open after an
await, which is why the flow never opened on /m.

Refresh now carries the row's stored auth_scheme to the provider, so an
api_key connection is re-initiated as api_key instead of managed OAuth.

fix(mobile): restore the tray when the agent hand-off navigation is cancelled

router.push resolves false for a cancelled navigation instead of throwing, so the agent overview composer skipped its failure cleanup: the stash stayed and, since the tray is now cleared up front, the attachment was gone. Handle both outcomes the way useHomeHandoff does.

The skills registry page always rendered the FilterRailLayout: title, search
and source facets in a second sidebar beside the app nav. That rail was
removed from every other desktop list page (#5833/#5846) and gated behind

fix(frontend): keep a failed agent lookup out of the automation editor's draft

A lookup that errored cleared the pending state without resolving, so the editor could seed its
draft with the variant id and write it back as the agent once a refetch recovered. The resolver
now reports pending and failed lookups alike as unsettled, and the editor waits per row.

fix(chat): write the per-session attachment store when the tray is cleared

clearAttachments reached the store only through the sync effect on the next commit. A hand-off navigates right after the call, and the destination composer seeds its tray from the store on mount, so the clear must land before that.

fix(mobile): put a voice take back in the tray when its send is refused

The refused-send path restored the tray snapshot only; a take uploaded through uploadExtraFiles never sat there and was lost. Restore the whole outbound set.

fix(mobile): send an automation's test run on landing and accept leaf agent ids

A test run opened a new session with the instruction drafted but unsent, so the reader
had to press Send to see the automation do anything (#6843). Both entry points — the
list row's menu and the detail screen's button — now hand the instruction to the chat
route through the Home `pendingTask` hand-off, so the run starts as the chat mounts.

SDK- and API-written triggers bind only a variant or a revision; the chat route looked that
id up as a workflow and, on the miss, rendered the session read-only. The lookup now falls
back to the variant and revision refs the backend already resolves, and reports the
revision's workflow id as the agent so nothing downstream sees a leaf id.

The instruction is the run, so an automation without one blocks with a reason instead of
opening an empty session.

[release] v0.118.1

fix(frontend): settle a durable send only after its records re-read has landed

When a run stream ended, useServerSessionInputs refreshed the dock, started
the host's records re-read without waiting for it, and reported the send
settled. Anything still waiting was flagged "Message wasn't sent" while the
read that would have retired it was in flight. Held back 45 s in the
browser, the note went up at 6.6 s under a message that was delivered and
answered. A connection that dropped after acceptance settled the same way,
though the turn may still be running.

Settlement now awaits the re-read and draws nothing from one that failed.
readRunAdmission reports acceptance and a self-ended stream separately, so
a dropped connection settles nothing. The chat package's re-read is a
fresh one (reloadSessionMessages marks the records stale first and resolves
once the refreshed log is delivered) instead of a cached read that answers
unchanged inside its stale window.

fix(mobile): send the Turnstile token on /m sign-in and show the region switch

On EE the API refuses every SuperTokens auth POST that carries no
x-turnstile-token, and /m never sent one, so Google/GitHub and email
sign-in all failed there (the desktop solves the widget and stamps the
header). Move the Turnstile seam (helper, widget, adapter hook) and the
cloud-region helpers/selector out of web/oss into @agenta/auth and
@agenta/auth-ui, repoint the desktop at them, and wire the /m forms and
the OIDC callback screen to the same adapter. /m/auth also gets the
EU/US data-residency switch it was missing.

fix(frontend): re-check the classic-mode hop to /m on every route change

useClassicModeRedirect only re-ran when the preference or the user
changed, but sign-in ends with a client-side push off /auth, where the
hook bails on purpose. A user with Classic mode off therefore signed in
and stayed on the desktop until a hard reload. Take the route as a key
so the hop fires once the push lands.

fix(frontend): acknowledge questionnaire submits in the docked card

The elicitation dock gave no feedback between pressing Send/Skip/Decline and the durable answer landing, so on a slow connection the tap looked ignored (#6812). Mirror ApprovalCard: track which button fired, spin it with LoadingButton and disable the rest until the write resolves or fails.

fix(api): allow Idempotency-Key in CORS preflight

Durable session writes (interaction answers, queued inputs) send Idempotency-Key, but the API's allow_headers did not list it, so every cross-origin client failed the preflight for /sessions/interactions/{id}/respond with 400 and the questionnaire answer never left the browser.

feat(frontend): render message toasts with Sonner

shadcn deprecated its Radix toast in favour of Sonner, so the message.* service now drives Sonner's toast() and the app-message outlet mounts shadcn's Toaster (ui/toast.tsx) themed through the --ag-* bridge: top-centre, status-coloured lucide icons, the secondary border. The hand-rolled antd-style Toast pill is gone. The antd handle contract stays — calling the handle closes, awaiting resolves on close, onClose fires once, a re-used key updates in place, duration 0 is sticky.

fix(services): keep dev-mode routes reachable when uvicorn sets root_path

The dev stacks run uvicorn with `--root-path /services`, which prepends the
prefix back onto `scope["path"]` after Traefik already stripped it. The strip
middleware consumed that head and left `root_path` untouched, so the `Mount`
subtraction Starlette does at every mount no longer lined up and every mounted
sub-app answered 404. Only the top-level `/health` route survived.

Strip only the part of the path that follows `root_path`, leaving the head in
place. The gh and cloud images run gunicorn with the uvicorn worker, which
leaves `root_path` empty, so their behavior is unchanged.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_015tSBrrUuBeqeJCj749WDPd

test(services): pin root_path as the servers, not the middleware's, to set

The strip may only ever shorten `path`. Rewriting `root_path` to match would
route just as well in the dev shape and would then hand every mounted sub-app a
mount point the server never published, so assert the narrower contract across
the three deployment shapes: managed ingress, uvicorn --root-path, and both.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_015tSBrrUuBeqeJCj749WDPd

fix(mobile): automation row actions run and open history on /m

The shared automations section published "Run in playground" to a seam only
the desktop chat panel consumed, so on /m the action did nothing. Mobile now
consumes that seam and starts a new session with the agent, the same hand-off
the automation detail screen uses.

Rename the row actions to "Test run" and "Run history"; the panel takes an
`onOpenRunHistory` slot so mobile navigates to the automation detail page on
its runs view (desktop keeps the deliveries drawer). Truncate the row subtitle
to one line.

fix(frontend): re-run the /m hop after a client-side navigation

Sign-in and the post-signup survey both leave through a client-side push, from
pages the classic-mode hop must skip (/auth, /post-signup). The middleware never
sees that navigation, and the hook only re-ran when the user or the preference

fix(runner): recover agent files when agent-files becomes a directory

The session workspace holds a symlink, agent-files, pointing at the agent's
durable drive. Delete it mid-turn and the harness's very next write recreates it
as an ordinary directory, because that is what writing agent-files/notes.md does
to a missing parent.

unlink(2) never removes a directory, so the repair failed with EISDIR on every
later turn and the link was never restored. Everything the agent then wrote to
what it believed was its durable drive piled up on the session workspace under
the same name. Nothing was lost, but nothing was where the agent or the person
reading the drive would look for it.

The repair now empties that directory onto the agent mount first, entry by
entry, keeping each name where it can and suffixing it with .recovered on a
collision, since a collision means the agent wrote the same name to both places
and neither copy is ours to discard. rmdir only succeeds on an empty directory,
so a rescue that moved less than everything cannot go on to delete the rest. If
the drive cannot take the files at all the directory is left exactly as it is
and the next turn tries again.

It also runs on every turn now. A warm environment is never re-acquired, so
mountLocalAgentCwd — until now the only caller — did not run on a second turn,
and a session that lost its link stayed broken for the life of its environment.
runTurn is the one function on both paths, so the repair moved there, placed
immediately after attachPermissionResponder because that function's invariant
forbids unconditional I/O above the responder attach.

Per turn rather than per tool call loses nothing. Writes made after a mid-turn
deletion land on the session drive, which is durable, and the repair moves them
onto the agent mount, so they arrive one turn late instead of never.

[AGE-4134] feat(frontend): run the connect step on mobile, and align its first run

Wires the pre-create connect step into /m behind the same
NEXT_PUBLIC_AGENT_CONNECT_STEP flag the desktop reads, via lib/connectStep.ts
(the browseLayout.ts precedent — mobile may not import @/oss/*).

/m's first run offered three plain text chips and a "Browse templates" button
where the desktop offers the real template strip. It now renders the shared
TemplateCard with the category filter and the desktop's composer placeholder:
a snap scroller on a phone, a three-across grid from lg up, so /m at desktop
width is a desktop layout rather than a phone scroller with cards running off
the right edge.

Four defects live QA caught that the unit tests did not:

- The footnote read "Nothing to do here." directly under two Connect buttons;
  setupStatus returns "ready" there and the copy fell through to the all-set
  line.
- Row subtitles truncated mid-word and every detected row repeated the same
  sentence. A detected row now carries no subtitle at all; the card's lead says
  where the rows came from once. Template rows keep their real scope line.
- Edit lost the description. The step REPLACES the composer, so setMarkdown ran
  against an unmounted editor; the text is parked and refilled on the render
  that remounts it.
- The lead claimed "From your description." for a template's declared accounts,
  which is false — that "description" is the builder message the user never
  wrote. setupLead now takes fromTemplate.

[AGE-4134] feat(frontend): give /m the playground-native onboarding

The desktop's first run redirects into a project-scoped playground on an
ephemeral agent (OnboardingEntry -> useAgentOnboarding) so the config pane is
live before anything exists: you see and change the model, instructions and
tools of the agent you are about to build. /m had none of that machinery — its
first run was a plain document that minted and committed on submit, so there
was nothing to inspect and nothing to change.

/m now mints the same local-only agent up front (useEphemeralAgent) and mounts
the real SessionWorkspace around it, with the create surface in the
conversation slot until the agent exists. The ephemeral is a normal entry in
the workflow molecule, so every entity-id-driven pane renders against it with
no special casing; only useAgentEntity's two queries cannot resolve a `local-*`
id, which is why the id is passed in rather than resolved from the session.

Submitting commits THAT ephemeral (createFromPrompt now takes entityId) instead
of minting a second one, so the agent the user configured is the agent they
get. The session id is minted once by the screen and shared with the composer,
which stages attachments against it, and with the workspace, which keys its
panes off it.

A failed mint reports itself with a retry that releases the once-guard, rather
than leaving the surface spinning — the desktop's equivalent path currently
hard-fails on a user-preference lookup and shows only "Couldn't set up your
agent".

[AGE-4134] fix(frontend): make /m first run render the real agent config

Four defects in the playground-native port, all found in the browser.

The config pane showed Advanced alone — no Model, Instructions, Tools or
Skills. The cause is not the mint: the ephemeral is fully seeded and
`/services/agent/v0/inspect` returns the right schema, whose `properties.agent`
carries `x-ag-type-ref: "agent-template"`. `parametersSchema` enriches such a
node by merging in that type's schema, but its query atom sits `pending`
forever on this surface — mounted, no request, no error — so the node stays a
bare stub with no properties and there are no fields to render. Seeding the
type schema under the same cache key gives the enrichment its data; the request
now fires (200, 5.9KB) and the pane renders Model and Instructions.

`deferInspect` is also dropped: the config pane is the point of this surface and
its sections are schema-driven, so the mint waits for the schema it displays.

Two nav rails: `SessionWorkspace` renders its own `AppShell` and Home already
wraps first run in one. It takes a `bare` prop now for hosts that provide the
shell themselves.

Editor placement: the create surface stacked from the top. Hero, then a flex
spacer, then templates and the composer docked at the bottom, as the desktop
does — with the named "Create agent" action in the composer's trailing slot
instead of a bare send arrow, and the desktop's category counts.

[AGE-4134] fix(frontend): stop the first-run template cards clipping

Two layout defects in the templates row, both measured in the browser.

The card's monogram overhangs its top edge by 20px and carries a 2px ring, so
`pt-5` left it flush: the ring sat 1px from the row's top and clipped. `pt-7`
gives it 9px of clearance.

The grid overflowed its container by 25px, cutting the cards off on the right.
A grid child defaults to `min-width: auto`, so the card's footer string
("2 GitHub tools · On release") set a min-content floor the track could not
shrink below. `lg:min-w-0` lets the columns size themselves; they now resolve to
three even 285px tracks inside the 880px column.

[AGE-4134] fix(frontend): stop template cards overflowing their grid track

The cards did not line up: in a three-column grid whose tracks measured an even
285.3px each, the cards themselves came out 307 / 295 / 311px, and each one's
right edge crossed its neighbour's left. Narrow categories were worse, because
the overflow scales with the footer string.

`TemplateCard` is a flex container, so it defaults to `min-width: auto` and its
own min-content width wins over the track it is placed in. `w-full min-w-0`
lets the track govern; the three cards now measure exactly 285px with even 12px
gaps, no overlap, and the `truncate`/`line-clamp` inside finally take effect
instead of pushing the box wider.

Verified in the browser across every category filter (3 cards, identical
widths, overlap=false) and in `TemplateGallery`, the other consumer, where all
28 cards render a uniform 435px with no overlap.

[AGE-4134] feat(frontend): drop the session tab strip from /m first run

fix(frontend): keep the config pane's visibility answerable per viewport and by intent

Two reports, one cause: whether the config pane shows was a single sticky global
that no context and no action could speak for.

#6378 — one localStorage key served every breakpoint. Opening the pane on a
desktop stores false, and a stored value beats the per-device default in both
directions, so the same browser at phone width opened the pane over the whole
screen and hid the playground. The preference is now per breakpoint; the wide
one keeps the original key, since a value stored before the split was almost
certainly set on a desktop and still means what it meant there.

#6381 — the agent overview's Edit navigated to the playground and nothing else,
so anyone who had ever collapsed the pane (or left Build/Chat maximized) landed
there with no configuration in sight and nothing saying why. Edit asks for the
configuration, so it now clears both things that hide it.

resolveConfigPanelCollapsed keeps its signature — only the choice of WHICH
stored answer to hand it moved — so the host default the onboarding surface
layers in is untouched.

feat(frontend): let /m edit an agent's configuration from its overview

The mobile overview passed no onEditConfig, commented 'configuration is edited in
the desktop playground'. That stopped being true: a session IS the playground on
/m, with the same config pane. The comment outlived the constraint, so the Edit
action was missing for no reason.

Edit opens a BLANK session for the agent — the id is client-side and nothing
reaches the backend until a message lands, so reading the configuration costs no
session (verified: the landing session is absent from /sessions/query).

The reveal itself moves into revealConfigPaneAtom, shared by both hosts' Edit.
Two persisted flags hide the pane and an action promising configuration has to
clear both; having written that logic twice was how #6381 could be fixed on one
surface and not the other.

fix(frontend): create the agent the composer describes now, not when the step opened

The connect step docks above the composer and leaves it editable, but Create
committed the seed captured when the step opened — an edit made while choosing
accounts was silently dropped, template provenance included. Re-read the live
composer at Create and resolve the template name against that text.

fix(frontend): only stop for the connect step when it has something to ask

Ashraf's report: writing a description and pressing Create produced a card
saying "We didn't spot a specific service in your description" and "Nothing
required." — a blocking step announcing it was not needed — with a second
"Create agent" button below it.

Two changes:

- open() now reports whether detection found anything, and every host commits
  straight through when it did not. The step interrupts only when there is a
  concrete account to connect, which is when the interruption pays for itself.
- the composer is hidden while the card is up, as it already is on /m. Leaving
  both up put two identically-labelled Create buttons on screen, and the
  composer's one merely re-opened the step it was already showing, so the
  button the user reaches for first appeared to do nothing.

feat(frontend): give a template's connections a role and alternatives

A template's providers were two hand-kept lists: requiredIntegrations (what
gates) and logoSlugs (what the card draws). Neither could say that GitLab
STANDS IN FOR GitHub, so the PR reviewer drew both marks, listed only GitHub,
and its setup step demanded GitHub of a GitLab user.

TemplateConnection names the slot by what the playbook needs it for and holds
the interchangeable options, which is what the playbooks have always said in
prose: "GitHub (or GitLab) to read the diff", "Slack or Discord are optional".

Card marks are now DERIVED from the slots, so a logo cannot advertise a
provider no slot accepts. Additive for now: templateConnections() reads an
unmigrated template as one required single-option slot per integration, so the
other 27 are untouched until they move over and the legacy fields go.

feat(frontend): render a connection slot as the choice it is

pr-reviewer now states its slot and nothing else — the legacy requiredIntegrations
twin is gone, because keeping both let a template disagree with itself: a test
fixture overrode the legacy field on a migrated template and the override was
silently ignored. Every consumer reads templateConnections() instead, so a
migrated and an unmigrated template are the same thing to a caller.

- the detail page labels a slot with every provider that satisfies it — GitHub
  or GitLab — and lists optional slots separately instead of dropping them
- detectAccountGroupsFromTemplate exposes the options so the setup card can
  offer the choice; the flat view keeps returning the primary, since an
  alternative rendered as a second row reads as more work, not a substitute
- tools front the primary option only, for the same reason

fix(frontend): let a card's primary provider win the overlap

The marks stack with a negative margin and no z-index, so the LAST badge painted
over the ones before it. The PR reviewer's alternative therefore covered its
primary and a small card read as GitLab — the provider the template does not
require.

Two halves:

- the stack now paints first-to-last, so the preferred provider stays legible
  and its alternatives peek out behind it
- templateProviderSlugs leads with the primary whatever order the hand-kept
  logo list is in. Five templates already drew a provider they do not require
  ahead of one they do: feedback-clusterer, meeting-followup, uptime-reporter,
  oncall-briefer and newsletter-drafter

templatePrimaryProvider names the rule so surfaces stop re-deriving it, and a
test holds every template to it rather than trusting array order to stay sorted.

fix(frontend): draw a brand logo on its own background, not the card's A mark was a bare . Brand logos are drawn for the brand's own backdrop, so a dark glyph — GitHub's — disappeared into a dark card and left the PR reviewer looking like a GitLab template, because the fox was the only mark still visible. The strip's badges already sat their logos on a light tile; LogoMarks now does the same, so the run reads on any surface in either theme.

Revert "fix(frontend): draw a brand logo on its own background, not the card's"

This reverts commit 74e25a76902163a454bda52869a60e1d057d40a0.

revert(frontend): restore the badge stack's original paint order

Reversing it so the primary sat on top was a look change nobody asked for. The
primary-first ordering from templateProviderSlugs stands on its own; how the
stack is drawn is a design call, not a side effect of a data fix.

fix(frontend): give a brand mark the ground it is drawn for

GitHub's logo is a black glyph on transparency, so on a dark card it read as
blank and the PR reviewer looked like a GitLab template. Longstanding, not a
regression: the mark has never had a background.

One class added, matching what IntegrationBadges already gives its logos, in
both themes. Geometry, size and radius are untouched.

feat(frontend): let an alternative satisfy the connection it stands in for

A workspace already on GitLab was still shown GitHub as the thing blocking
Create, because a row could only query its own provider — nothing could see
that the need was already met by a stand-in.

- an account carries the slugs that satisfy it instead of its own only, so
  gating asks "is this NEED met" rather than "is this provider connected"
- the card reads the project's connections once and hands each row the provider
  already meeting it; a row settles on sight instead of asking again
- one row per need, not per provider: two rows joined by "or" read as two
  things to connect, which is the opposite of what a choice means

DetectedAccountGroup is gone — it and the alternatives field were two models
for one idea, and the flat row is the one every surface already renders.

feat(frontend): say the choice out loud, and stop asking what is already answered

Two halves of the same idea — the step should only spend attention on something
genuinely missing.

- the row names the alternatives it accepts ("or GitLab"), so the choice exists
  in the UI and not only in the data, and when a stand-in settles the row it is
  that provider's name shown, not a claim to one the workspace has not got
- open() consults the workspace's connections and declines when every required
  need is already met. A returning user picking a template they are connected
  for lands on their agent instead of a card of ticked rows and a button.

Together with the earlier empty-detection gate, the step now interrupts only
when there is something to ask.

refactor(frontend): a slot has one primary and the slugs that stand in for it

options[] implied every alternative carried a scope line and a tool list. The
playbooks name none of that — "or GitLab" and nothing more — so migrating 27
templates against it would have meant inventing product data for each. It
already had: pr-reviewer's GitLab tools were written by analogy, by me, and are
now gone.

The primary keeps the scope and tools it is written against; an alternative is
a slug, which is exactly what the source says.

feat(frontend): move all 28 templates onto connection slots

Each slot's role and required/optional split is read from that template's own
playbook prose, so the UI now mirrors the source instead of paraphrasing it:
62 slots, 42 required, 36 carrying an alternative.

Two consequences worth naming:

- changelog-writer gains a second REQUIRED slot. Its playbook has always said
  "and the publish target (docs repo, Notion, or Linear) ... if any is missing,
  request_connection and stop", but the old list named only GitHub, so the page
  understated what the agent needs and Create never gated on it.
- logoSlugs and requiredIntegrations are gone. Card marks derive from the slots,
  so the drift they allowed — five templates leading with a provider they do not
  require, an alternative that existed only as a logo — is now unrepresentable.

tools is optional: a slot the playbook names without naming its calls has none,
which is honest. The alternative was inventing them.

test(frontend): hold the catalogue to the playbooks it mirrors

The catalogue describes a template to the user and the playbook describes it to
the builder agent; nothing generated one from the other, so nothing noticed
them drifting. This asserts both halves define the same 28 templates, and that
every provider a slot names appears in that template's Connections prose.

It failed on first run against my own migration: I had promoted six decorative
logoSlugs into real slots — support-triage's ticket source, support-reply-drafter's
review channel, lead-qualifier's notify target, bug-report-router's zendesk,
knowledge-chatbot's confluence and drive, weekly-report's linear — none of which
their playbooks mention. Promoting decoration into meaning is the failure this
whole change exists to remove, so they are gone.

Two pre-existing divergences stay, listed and explained rather than asserted
away: uptime-reporter and oncall-briefer require Slack while their playbooks
name only Sentry. Dropping a required connection is a product call.

fix(frontend): create the agent when the connect step declines to open

open() now reports whether it had anything to ask, but both call sites here
returned unconditionally — so once the step started declining (nothing detected,
or the workspace already connected), picking a template or describing an agent
returned without creating anything. The click did nothing at all.

Both paths fall through to create when the step declines, which is the point of
the gate: skip the question, not the agent.

fix(frontend): make every template pick ask for the same connections

Picking a template asked to connect on some surfaces and silently skipped it on
others — and the surfaces that skipped were the ones that knew most precisely
what was needed, since a template DECLARES its connections.

Before: first-run gallery pick asked; a returning user's pick only seeded a
composer; "Use this template" created immediately; on /m the detail screen and
the New agent menu both created immediately. Four paths, three behaviours.

Now every pick runs the same gate, wherever it starts:

- the desktop detail page hands the pick to the create surface, the route the
  gallery already used for a returning user
- arriving there with ?template= is treated as the pick it was, rather than
  seeding a composer the user must then submit
- /m's detail screen hosts the step, replacing the detail while it is open, as
  the step replaces the composer on first run
- /m's New agent menu opens the template instead of creating from it: a menu has
  nowhere to show the step, and the detail screen already asks

The gate still declines when there is nothing to ask, so a workspace already
connected goes straight to its agent.

revert(frontend): do not open the connect step on arrival

Treating ?template= as a pick opened the step on a surface that had just seeded
its composer, so the page showed the hero asking for a description, a template

The composer keeps the seed and the step comes on submit, as before. Routing the

fix(frontend): keep Use this template building the agent

Routing the pick to the create surface stopped it doing the one thing it says:

The step belongs on the detail page instead — it replaces the detail while open,

revert(frontend): leave the template detail page as it was

Three attempts at putting the connect step on this page, three wrong shapes: a

Back to what it was. The gap it leaves is the one it always had: this page
creates without asking to connect.

fix(frontend): put the connect step back on the template detail page

Reverting it removed the card this work exists to show: picking PR reviewer
went straight to a playground with no chance to connect GitHub. The revert was

Restored as it was: the step replaces the detail while open, creates with what

fix(frontend): show the connect card where the composer was

The card belongs at the bottom, in the composer's place — the shape agreed for
Ashraf's report. I had put it on the template detail page instead, where there
is no composer, so it sat alone at the top of an empty page.

- the detail page hands the pick to the create surface, which renders the card

- arriving there with ?template= opens the step, so a pick made on another page

- the provenance chip hides while the step is open: it docks onto the composer's

fix(frontend): hide the chip on the surface the step actually replaces

The previous commit put the condition on the workspace home's composer, where
the step never opens, and left the create surface's chip rendering — so the chip

feat(frontend): let the hero speak about the template it is setting up

The generic hero asks "What do you want to build?" — the question a template
pick has already answered, above a description of exactly what is being built.
A template names itself and asks the one thing still open: what to connect.

Blank creates keep the original hero; only a pick changes it.

Spacing: the gap under the hero was sized for a chip docking into it, and the

the card are one block and now sit like one — closer together, and the line
inset to the card's own edge so they share a left margin.

feat(frontend): send first run to the create surface, not a second one

Describing an agent happened on two surfaces with two behaviours. First run was
redirected to the ephemeral onboarding playground, where the connect step docked
ABOVE a live composer — so the user faced two "Create agent" buttons, which is
the report this work started from. Everyone else got the agent-home create
surface, where the step replaces the composer instead.

First run now lands on the same create surface as everyone else. One surface,
one behaviour, and the flow Ashraf hit no longer exists rather than being
patched in two places.

feat(frontend): let the template's own prompt carry the page

The generic subtitle explained the step to a user who had already chosen it, and
the prompt sat in a "Building" line between the hero and the card — three blocks
competing above the one thing to answer.

The prompt now reads as the subtitle, so the page says what is being built in
the template's own words. The connect card centres in the frame as the only
thing asked for. The prompt also sits read-only at the bottom, where the composer
docks, with Edit to reopen it for typing — present as the thing being built,
not as a field to fill in here.

feat(frontend): let a host dock content inside the composer frame

Two seams the create surface needs from the chat package.

`ChatComposer` gains `headerExtra`, rendered inside the input frame above
the attachments tray — for host content that belongs to the message being
composed, not floating beside it. The connect step's card is the first user.

`configPanelCollapsedOverrideAtom` is a mount-scoped, unpersisted override
for a surface that must LAND with the config pane collapsed whatever the
session pages stored. Any user write through `configPanelCollapsedAtom`
clears it, so the reveal button works on the first click and the stored
preference takes over from that moment.

feat(frontend): name a connection by its need, and drop skip

Three changes to the setup model, all pushing the same way: a slot is a NEED
answered by a provider, not a provider.

`PROVIDER_CATEGORY` + `connectionNeedLabel` give a slot whose options share
one category its own name ("Source control", "CRM"). A choice slot titled by
its preferred provider misleads — "HubSpot · Optional" over a
HubSpot/Salesforce/Attio choice reads as a HubSpot requirement. Mixed-category
slots keep the provider name, and text-detected accounts never get one: there
the user named the provider themselves.

`skippedSlugs` is gone from `AgentSetupSelection`. An optional slot left
unconnected IS the skip — the builder asks when it needs it, so no button had
to say so, and `setupStatus` no longer has a skipped set to reconcile.

`buildSetupPreamble` now resolves each account through its ALTERNATIVES, so a
GitHub|GitLab slot connected via GitLab reports GitLab. It also states a
non-primary choice as an instruction ("Use GitLab, not GitHub."): the choice
travels only as prose, and prose loses to the template's own vocabulary when
both providers hold live connections and tool discovery offers each.

feat(frontend): let the connect card offer the choice, not just the requirement

The card now renders one selectable provider card per option, so choosing and
connecting are a single act: tapping an unconnected option opens ITS connect
drawer, tapping a connected one makes it the provider this agent uses. The ring
marks what is in use; the template's preference is carried by ORDER, primary
first, not by a label. A single-provider slot renders its one card too — the row
is titled by the need ("Email"), so the card is where Gmail shows its face.

`useAgentSetupStep.open()` no longer declines just because every required slot
is satisfied: a template slot offering a CHOICE still opens, or a workspace on
GitHub could never build the GitLab twin. Whether the draft came from a template
is held separately from the draft itself — gating suggestions on `draft?.template`
made them reappear the instant `close()` nulled it, growing the card mid-fold.

Skip is gone with the model change: leaving an optional slot unconnected IS the
skip.

`ConnectDrawer` now surfaces a failed create. It said nothing before — the
spinner just stopped, indistinguishable from a popup that never opened.

An unpinned session resolved "the agent's latest revision" through a

fix(hosting): drop --root-path from the dev services container

Every mounted sub-app under the services container answered 404 to an
authenticated request. /services/health worked, so the container looked fine,
but /services/agent/v0/* — invoke, inspect, runtime/subscription-status — all
returned {"detail":"Not Found"}. On /m that surfaces as an agent that is
created and then cannot run: the first message comes back "was not sent".

The prefix is handled twice already. Traefik strips /services before the
request reaches the container (services-strip), and the app strips it again
itself for ingresses that cannot rewrite paths
(ServicesPrefixStripMiddleware, added in #6702). Passing --root-path /services
on top of that breaks routing into the Mount()ed sub-apps.

Proved by running the same app inside the same container on a second port
without the flag: the identical authenticated request returns 200 with a live
runner body for both /agent/v0/... and /services/agent/v0/... path shapes.

The api container keeps its --root-path /api: it has no mounted sub-apps, so
the same interaction does not arise there.

feat(mobile): carry the template key from Home's composer too

Home's template rows bound the composer to a whole template but sent only its
NAME on submit, so a template picked there was the one create path the session
could not gate: the key never reached the stashed task, and the connect step
had nothing to look up.

HomeFocus already read binding.template.key a few lines below, so this is that
same value through three signatures — HomeFocus, useHomeHandoff, and
createFromPrompt, which hands it to run() where templateKey was already
supported and already stashed.

Free text on Home stays ungated on purpose. It declares no accounts, the
builder decides its tools during the very turn being held, and the mid-run
connect dock covers what it turns out to need.

All four create paths now behave the same: template entries ask for the
template's accounts in the session, free text does not, and the step runs in
exactly one place.

test(mobile): cover what the in-session connect step decides and holds

Six cases for useSessionSetupStep, the one piece of this flow with no coverage.
The step's own rules live in useAgentSetupStep and are tested in entity-ui;
what is this hook's own is narrower and is what these assert: it reads the
template key off the stashed task, waits for the connections query before
deciding, and reports blocking so the held first message is not sent under it.

The two that would bite in production: a session with no template never holds,
and a step that declines to open releases at once rather than parking a message
behind a card that never appears.

Note for anyone running these: use `pnpm exec vitest`, not `npx vitest`. npx
resolves the workspace-root vitest, which has no jsdom, and the seven jsdom
suites are then skipped silently — 28 files instead of 35.

perf(drive): edit caps, keystrokes stay inside the editor body

Stress-tested on /m with generated files. Before: a 272 KB / 2 000-line JS
file took 2.7 s to open and 260 ms per keystroke; 1.4 MB took 17 s and
540 MB of heap; even a 5 KB file cost ~50 ms per keystroke because every
edit re-rendered DriveExplorer.

- Files over 96 KB (code) / 512 KB (markdown) open read-only in the
  preview, with a note in row 2.
- The draft hook splits: the explorer watches a derived dirty atom and a
  store subscription for the autosave timer (no render per keystroke); the
  editor bodies read the draft themselves.
- The code editor mounts on the seed, not the live value, so the code
  plugin stops re-reading the whole document per keystroke.

After: a keystroke in a 5 KB file renders only the editor body with no
long task; 80 KB: 64 ms per keystroke (the shared editor's own
serialisation), 56 ms per autosave; 272 KB opens read-only in 57 ms.

feat(gateways): opt-in for plain-HTTP gateways, and a typed refusal (OR24, OR25)

D37 lets a gateway bearer credential travel over https, or over a loopback hop that
has no remote to leak it to. That left one deployment shape unable to use a gateway
at all: a self-hosted instance reached at a plain-http address that is not loopback,
an IP or a LAN name. Every gateway-routed run failed, because the credential could
not be sent to the deployment's own base URL.

Two problems, one cause.

The rule was applied inconsistently. The SDK refused a routable plain-http gateway
while the runner accepted one, and the runner's loopback set omitted
`host.docker.internal`, which the SDK has always treated as loopback. A connection
could pass one leg and be refused by the other.

The refusal was untyped. It surfaced as a pydantic ValidationError escaping
`ResolvedConnection`, which the running normalizer could only report as an unhandled
500 with a traceback, so an operator whose only mistake was serving over plain http
saw a server fault and no way to act on it.

AGENTA_GATEWAYS_INSECURE_HTTP_ALLOWED, default off, is the opt-in a trusted
single-tenant deployment sets, following AGENTA_INSECURE_EGRESS_ALLOWED's precedent.
It is deliberately narrow: it covers only our own credentials into our own gateway.
A provider's own secret keeps D37's rule unconditionally, since the reason there is a
host we do not control, and the Daytona credential-endpoint rules are untouched,
since a remote sandbox dials across the internet. Both legs now read the same
variable and share one loopback set.

GatewayInsecureEndpointError carries the agent-actionable envelope the runner already
recovers from a gateway data-plane refusal: code `gateway_insecure_endpoint`,
retryable false, a next_step naming the variable, and the gateway base URL in
details. It is raised at `build_gateway_resolved_connection`, the seam every gateway
connection passes through. The model validator keeps raising underneath it: that is
the invariant no construction path can dodge.

The variable has to be declared explicitly on the runner in every compose file. That
service has no env_file on purpose, and the runner is the leg that re-validates the
transport rule, so a value set for the api and services but not there would admit a
run and then strand it inside the sandbox.

Two existing expectations change, both because they encoded the inconsistency. The
runner case asserting a routable plain-http host was accepted now asserts the
loopback route it was named for, and the SDK case expecting a bare ValueError now
expects the typed error.

fix(gateways): pin the authorization server, refresh expired grants, let the database arbitrate (OR42, OR55, OR61)

OR42. Discovery took the authorization and token endpoints verbatim from the upstream's own
metadata, so a hostile or compromised MCP server could name its own token endpoint and
receive the user's authorization code together with Agenta's registered client secret.
Three checks now chain back to what the tenant registered: the protected-resource metadata
must describe a resource same-origin with the registered server URL, the authorization
server's metadata issuer must equal the server that document named, and all three endpoints
must be same-origin with that issuer. HTTPS is required throughout, gated on the gateway's
own egress flag rather than a second switch.

Same-origin on the endpoints goes beyond RFC 8414, deliberately, because the split is the
attack: the honest server mints the code and holds the client secret, and a document naming
a foreign token endpoint sends both somewhere else. The cost is that an authorization server
which splits its endpoints across origins, in the style of Google's, cannot be used, and it
is refused with the offending origin named. What this does not stop is a hostile MCP server
naming an authorization server it owns outright, because that flow is self-consistent and
the user sees the attacker's own login page. Pinning answers where an issuer lives, never
whether it is honest. Upstream bodies no longer reach user-visible errors either, which is
what turned any discovery weakness into a read primitive; the text is now the status and the
origin, and the validation-error strings that carried the body are gone.

kept reporting READY while every call failed. An expired or nearly expired grant is now
exchanged and stored before use, through the shared egress client. A lock per project and

was preferred whenever this deployment is publicly resolvable, and dynamic client
registration was used only when it is not. That document is a draft almost nothing
implements, so an authorization server handed one sees a client id it never issued and
refuses. Registration is RFC 7591 and is what this ecosystem supports: Linear advertises a
registration endpoint and expects it to be used. The old order therefore picked the draft
strategy precisely where the standard one was available, which is every deployment that can
complete a consent flow at all, so no real server could ever be connected.

The order is now a stored registration, then registration when the server advertises an
endpoint for it, then the identity document when it advertises none and we are publicly
reachable, then a refusal naming the reason when neither is possible. The document keeps
the job it is actually good for: a server that cannot be registered with, where a public
document is the only way to name ourselves.

advertises no registration endpoint, which is the condition that makes the document
correct, and they keep every assertion they had; one gained an assertion that nothing
reached the registration endpoint. A fourth test's name attributed its outcome to the
deployment being private, which is no longer what drives that path, so it now says what it
tests.
